findings.finding_value: The semantic range of the cluster's vocabulary is exceptionally broad: from physical fat/richness (sha.men — the literal fatness of animals and persons) through material wealth (o.sher, hon, cho.sen — various aspects of material goods) through the inner condition of prosperity or poverty (da.shen applied to ne.phesh — inner richness; ptōchos tō pneumati — poverty in spirit) through eschatological and Christological wealth (plousios applied to Christ, ploutos applied to the riches of grace and glory in Ephesians) through the philosophical-theological concept of self-sufficient contentment (autarkēs). The semantic range spans the physical, material, inner, relational, divine, eschatological, and philosophical registers — confirming that the wealth vocabulary in Scripture is not confined to economics but extends into every register of meaning.

ya.re (H3372-3374) spans: (a) the reverential posture before God (the large majority of M01-A uses); (b) the acute alarm before threat (M01-B-VCG-03; M01-B-VCG-05 where ya.re terms appear with M01-B routing); (c) the reactive fear at unexpected events (Gen 28:17: Jacob afraid at the divine place); (d) the commanded prohibition of fear ("do not be afraid" — ya.re in M01-B-VCG-06 corpus). The semantic range is extremely broad — a single root covers the full spectrum from cringing alarm to the highest reverential posture of the worshipper. This breadth is itself analytically significant: Hebrew does not distinguish reverential fear from acute alarm at the root level; the distinction is contextual.

**[Folded from wa_session_b_findings.id=67; finding_id=DIM-61-001; registry=fear]**
fobeō (G5399) shows a tripartite inner-being structure: (1) theophanic/miraculous fear leading to worship (Spiritual/God-ward), (2) reverential life-shaping fear of God (Spiritual/God-ward), (3) practical self-interested fear before humans or consequences (Affective/Emotional). This tripartite structure is the most analytically important pattern in Registry 61 and should be the organising frame for Session B analysis.

ra.gaz (H7264) spans: (a) trembling of persons in fear (M01-E-VCG-01, 04); (b) trembling of the earth in theophany (set aside — outside inner-being scope); (c) inner agitation and distress (2Sa 18:33: David's grief "shook his inner being violently"); (d) rousing/stirring to action (set aside uses). The semantic range covers bodily fear-trembling, inner agitation, and arousal to action — a broad root used across multiple registers.

The primary terms of M01 are semantically broad: ya.re spans reverential awe to cringing alarm; pa.chad spans covenant-name for God (Gen 31:42) to the dread of nocturnal terror (Psa 91:5); ra.gaz spans inner distress to cosmic earth-trembling. This semantic breadth reflects the cluster's genuine scope: fear in Scripture is not a narrow technical term but a broad characterisation of the person's oriented-response to power.

*Che.mah* (H2534, 110 verses) has the widest semantic range in the cluster: (1) rage filling and possessing (Est 3:5); (2) stored and discharged divine wrath (Eze 5:13); (3) covenant discipline (Lev 26:28); (4) rage as relational signal (2Ki 5:12 — Naaman's contemptuous indignation); (5) rage as social contagion risk (Pro 22:24); (6) rage as jealousy-driven (Pro 6:34); (7) rage as the recipient's experience of being under wrath (Job 6:4). The range is: inner emotional episode → sustained character-state → stored judicial force → physically experienced consequence. *Orgē* (G3709, 33 verses) also has wide range: human anger that must be restrained (Jam 1:19) → divine eschatological wrath (Rev 19:15) → settled abiding condition (Joh 3:36) → institutional-judicial force (Rom 13:4).

For ba.khah (the most extensive primary term, 99 verses — M03-A): the semantic range spans from genuine bereavement grief to manipulative weeping (Judg 14:16-17, flagged) to weeping of craving/discontent (Num 11:4-20, flagged). The range reveals that ba.khah is a broad weeping term that describes the outward act of weeping without specifying its inner quality or moral status — it is the word for weeping regardless of what drives it. For tsa.rah (the second most extensive, 62 verses — M03-D): the range spans from personal distress (Gen 42:21) to siege-catastrophe (Deu 31:17) to eschatological day-of-trouble (Dan 12:1). The range reveals tsa.rah as a term that scales across the full spectrum of adversity — personal to cosmic.

The range reveals tsa.rah as a term that scales across the full spectrum of adversity — personal to cosmic.

**[CHAR-1]** E — **gil** (verbal and nominal) ranges across: (1) human rejoicing directed at God (primary: Psa 32:11; 35:9; 89:16; 97:1); (2) God's rejoicing over his people (Zep 3:17; Isa 65:19; Jer 32:41); (3) human relational rejoicing (Pro 23:24–25; Song 1:4; Isa 9:3); (4) creation's personified rejoicing (Psa 96:11; 97:1; Isa 35:1–2; 49:13); (5) inverted/absent rejoicing (Psa 13:4; Pro 24:17; Joe 1:16; Jer 48:33; Hos 10:5); (6) prohibited or illegitimate rejoicing (Hos 9:1; Pro 2:14; Pro 24:17). The full semantic range shows exultation as a comprehensive inner-being capacity that can operate in any direction, including corrupted ones.

**[CHAR-2]** E — **sa.mach** ranges across: (1) prescribed feast-joy (Deu 12:7; 16:11–15 — commanded worship context); (2) responsive-spontaneous joy (Exo 4:14 — heart-gladness; 1Sa 6:13 — joy at seeing the ark); (3) relational/parental joy (Pro 10:1; 23:24–25 — father's joy at wise son); (4) God-directed psalmist joy (Psa 5:11; 9:2; 14:7; 32:11; 40:16 — rejoice in the Lord); (5) inverted/corrupt joy (Pro 2:14; Eze 25:6; Hos 9:1; Jon 4:6 — rejoicing at evil or wrongly-directed); (6) God himself rejoicing (Isa 65:19; Psa 104:31; Jer 32:41 — divine joy). The range is broader than any other term in M04 — sa.mach covers every register of Joy from prescribed worship to personal gladness to divine inner life to corrupt misdirection.

**[CHAR-7]** E — agalliao ranges across: (1) **Mary's spirit-exultation** (Luk 1:47 — Spirit-joy in vulnerability); (2) **Jesus' Spirit-rejoicing** (Luk 10:21 — divine-human rejoicing in the Holy Spirit); (3) **Abraham's anticipatory faith-joy** (Joh 8:56 — prophetic exultation at Christ's day); (4) **The body's hope-residing** (Act 2:26 — tongue agalliao alongside bodily hope); (5) **Persecuted community's commanded joy** (Mat 5:12; Luk 6:23); (6) **Trials-joy** (1Pe 1:6 — alongside grieving trials); (7) **Suffering-glory orientation** (1Pe 4:13 — insofar as sharing Christ's sufferings); (8) **Faith-without-sight joy** (1Pe 1:8 — inexpressible and glorious); (9) **Coming-to-faith joy** (Act 16:34); (10) **Eschatological wedding joy** (Rev 19:7). The range shows agalliao operating across the full span from intimate-Spirit-joy to communal-eschatological-joy, always with the quality of intensity that distinguishes it from ordinary chairo.

**[CHAR-3]** E — tov's semantic range is the widest of any M04 primary term: (1) **Divine character** — "the Lord is good" (M04-L-VCG-01 — intrinsic divine attribute); (2) **Moral quality** — "a good man" (M04-L-VCG-02 — human moral character); (3) **Evaluative judgment** — "better than" (M04-L-VCG-02, VCG-03 — comparative moral or wisdom assessments); (4) **Circumstantial benefit** — "good news," "it will be well with you," "good land" (M04-O — situational goodness); (5) **Covenantal promise-quality** — "good promises," "good hand" (M04-O-VCG-04 — divine reliable provision); (6) **Wellbeing** — "Saul was well" (1Sa 16:23 — experiential inner wellbeing). This breadth confirms tov as the programme's most foundational positive-quality term.

**[CHAR-4]** E — cha.phets/che.phets ranges across: (1) **Divine sovereign will** — Psa 115:3; 135:6; Isa 44:28; 46:10; 53:10; 55:11 — God's cha.phets as his operative purpose; (2) **Divine relational delight in persons** — Psa 18:19; 37:23; 51:6; Jer 9:24; Hos 6:6; Mic 7:18; (3) **Human strong personal desire** — Gen 34:19; Psa 73:25; Job 13:3; 1Ki 9:1; (4) **Human volitional preference in practical/diplomatic contexts** — the entire M04-H-VCG-03 diplomatic idiom; (5) **Negated pleasure** — Psa 5:4; Heb 10:6, 8; Jer 6:10; Mal 1:10; (6) **Love's own readiness** — Song 2:7; 3:5; 8:4. Semantic range runs from the most transcendent (God's sovereign will) to the most mundane (diplomatic preference) through the most intimate (love's readiness). The range is unique in M04.

**[CHAR-5]** E — na.im/na.em/no.am ranges across: (1) **Divine character** — Psa 27:4 (God's own beauty/pleasantness); (2) **Relational warmth** — 2Sa 1:26 (Jonathan's pleasantness to David); Psa 133:1 (brotherly unity's pleasantness); (3) **Wisdom's character** — Pro 3:17 (wisdom's ways as pleasantness); (4) **Speech** — Pro 15:26; 16:24 (gracious words as pleasant); (5) **Praise** — Psa 135:3; 147:1 (praise as pleasant); (6) **Creation** — Psa 16:6 (pleasant places); (7) **Negative** — Pro 9:17 (stolen bread appearing pleasant — the only morally negative instance within this vocabulary). The semantic range is primarily positive-relational and aesthetic, with the negative instance (Pro 9:17) being the exception that proves the rule.

**[CHAR-6]** E — pa.la ranges across: (1) **Divine wonder-acts** — Exo 3:20; 34:10; Psa 78:4; 86:10; 136:4; (2) **Human Wonder-response** — Psa 118:23; 139:14; 119:18; (3) **Cognitive-limit naming** — Deu 17:8 ("too difficult"); 30:11 ("not too hard"); Gen 18:14 ("is anything too hard?"); Job 42:3 ("too wonderful for me"); (4) **Dark-Wonder** — Job 10:16 (wonders worked against Job); Deu 28:59 (extraordinary afflictions); Dan 8:24; 11:36; (5) **Extraordinary love** — 2Sa 1:26 (Jonathan's love as pa.la); (6) **Divine name-quality** — Isa 9:6 (Wonderful Counselor). Semantic range confirms pa.la as the most versatile Wonder term, covering positive, negative, cognitive-limit, and name-quality registers.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The comparative semantic ranges confirm that **tov** (Gladness, Char 3) has the widest semantic range of any primary term in the cluster — spanning divine character, moral quality, comparative evaluation, circumstantial benefit, and covenant goodness. This breadth is consistent with Gladness's status as the most cognitively-primary characteristic: the term that names genuine goodness in all its registers is the broadest term in the cluster. By contrast, **pa.la** (Wonder, Char 6) is the most semantically focused — it names what is categorically set apart from ordinary reality — which is consistent with Wonder's specific cognitive-perceptive function at the boundary of comprehension. **cha.phets/che.phets** (Delight, Char 4) spans the widest range of actors (God's sovereign will → human personal preference → diplomatic deference) — consistent with Delight's status as the most constitutionally and sociologically distributed characteristic in the cluster.

**[CHAR-1]** E — *Bosh* ranges from acute momentary shame (the servants covering heads before drought) to chronic existential shame ("spend my days in shame") to moral shame-as-consequence (the wicked clothed with shame) to shame-before-God (Ezr 9:6) to cosmic shame (even the moon will be ashamed, Isa 24:23). The semantic range is almost the entire register of human inner moral exposure — making *bosh* one of the most semantically broad shame-vocabulary items in the evidence. *Ke.lim.mah* is narrower: primarily the social-facing, communally-visible disgrace, the ongoing wound of being seen as dishonoured.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Ka.lam operates primarily as a verb (being humiliated). Sha.phel operates as verb (Hiphil — causing to be brought low) and adjective (sha.phel nefesh — lowly of spirit). The verbal dominance confirms CHAR-2's action-character: it is something done, not merely something possessed. Semantic range covers bodily-social, national-political, and cosmic dimensions (moon and sun ashamed, Isa 24:23) — CHAR-2 applies wherever pride-structures or elevated standing exists.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — Primary terms: Atimazō (G0818): to dishonour, treat as without honour — active verb, the dishonoring act. Atimia (G0819): dishonour as a state — the condition of assigned or received diminished worth. Entrepō (G1788) in its absence register: the failure of the regard-faculty. Paradeigmatizō (G3856): to expose publicly, hold up to contempt. Roots: a-timē — without honour, without worth — the alpha-privative of honour. Structural opposite: timaō (to honour, to assign worth) and timē (honour as assigned worth-recognition). The evidence pairs these explicitly in Joh 8:49. The CHAR-3 corpus is entirely NT — the OT vocabulary for relational worth-denial (qa.lah, H7034; entrepō in its absence register) is thinner. The NT's christological context gives CHAR-3 its sharpest definition: dishonour as what is directed at Jesus personally and at God through human hypocrisy. Person-type: the "unjust judge" (Luk 18:2) is the closest person-type but is not a technical term. Supplication: the widow's persistent coming to the judge (Luk 18:3) is a supplication for the reversal of CHAR-3 — the only supplication-context in the corpus.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — Aischros is consistently adjectival — it modifies conduct, gain, or situations. Aschēmosunē is consistently nominal — naming the quality. The adjectival/nominal dominance confirms CHAR-4's quality-character: it is about the property of things (shameful conduct, indecent acts) rather than the experience of persons. The semantic range is limited: all primary CHAR-4 terms specifically name the quality of moral shamefulness — they do not range into the social-status register of the shame vocabulary.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — Exoutheneō operates as a verb (to despise, to treat as nothing). Atimazō operates as a verb (to dishonour, to treat shamefully). Loidoria is a noun (reviling, verbal abuse). The verbal dominance confirms CHAR-5's action-character: the contempt is always something done — an active verbal or physical or attitudinal act. The semantic range spans inner attitude (VCG-01 — the exoutheneō of the self-righteous), physical violence (VCG-02 — the atimazō of violent treatment), and verbal assault (VCG-03 — the loidoria of reputation-attack).

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — Both terms function primarily as nouns naming a condition: "in the innocence of my hands" (Gen 20:5; Psa 26:6) — the innocence is a quality of the hands named nominally. The nominal form confirms CHAR-6's quality-character: innocence is a condition the person possesses (or fails to possess), not a direction or act. The semantic range of niq.qa.von is narrow within this corpus: it specifically names the moral cleanness that enables approach to God and protects against guilt-shame. It does not range into the social-status vocabulary of shame's other terms.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's primary vocabulary is distributed across three grammatical categories: stative verbs (bosh — being ashamed; sha.phel — being brought low) name the experienced conditions (Chars 1, 2); transitive verbs (atimazō — to dishonour; exoutheneō — to despise) name the enacted acts (Chars 3, 5); adjectives/nouns (aischros — shameful; niq.qa.von — innocence; atimia — dishonour as a noun) name the evaluative quality and its counter (Chars 4, 6). This grammatical distribution mirrors the cluster's characteristic diversity: conditions are expressed statically, enacted acts transitively, and qualities adjectivally/nominally. Semantic range: from the acute personal shame of the psalmist (bosh in Psa 44:15) to the cosmic shame of the moon and sun before divine glory (bosh in Isa 24:23), and from the intimate hand-washing innocence (niq.qa.von in Psa 26:6) to the incapacity-for-innocence of an entire people (niq.qa.von in Hos 8:5). M07 applies its vocabulary at every level of human existence.

---

**[CHAR-1]** E — The rum (H7311A/H7312) root has the widest semantic range of any CHAR-1 term, operating across four distinct meaning registers evidenced in the broader biblical corpus: (a) CHAR-1 register — human arrogant self-elevation (Deu 8:14, vc=34223; Isa 14:13, vc=34233; Dan 11:36, vc=34235 — the current corpus); (b) M22 register — divine exaltation and genuine majesty (the 122 set-aside M22-register rum verses confirm this range is present in the same term); (c) God-lifting-up the humble — the righteous lifted up by God's act (Psa 75:10, vc=34264, M08-A4-VCG-05: "the horns of the righteous shall be lifted up" — God as the agent); (d) Providential elevation of the Israelite community out of Egypt (Exo 14:8, vc=34239, M08-A4-VCG-05: going out "with a high hand" — bold, God-enabled). The g-'-h root similarly ranges from human pride (M08 register) to divine majesty (M22 register). The semantic range of the primary terms encompasses the full elevation spectrum — from the creature's illegitimate self-elevation (CHAR-1), through God's proper exaltation of the humble, to God's own genuine majesty (M22).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Zid operates across two primary semantic registers within the biblical corpus: (a) CHAR-2 register — wilful presumptuous transgression of a divine limit (Deu 1:43; Deu 18:20; Neh 9:10/16/29; Jer 50:29 — the current corpus); (b) physical cooking sense — "the pottage he was boiling" (Gen 25:29) — the physical boiling from which the metaphor derives. The semantic range is narrower than CHAR-1's rum/ga.on terms: zid's primary figurative meaning in the Hebrew Bible is specifically the presumptuous, wilful quality of transgression, without the broader range across divine majesty and legitimate elevation. This narrower semantic range confirms CHAR-2 as a more specifically targeted characteristic than CHAR-1's broader elevation vocabulary.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Kauchaomai has the widest semantic range of any CHAR-3 term, spanning: (a) condemned self-directed boasting (VCG-01: Rom 2:17, vc=33882: boasting in the law while breaking it; 1Cor 1:29, vc=33877: the boasting that God's election is designed to eliminate); (b) Pauline examined self-commendation (VCG-02: 2Cor 10:13, vc=33888: bounded boasting within God-assigned sphere; 2Cor 12:9, vc=33870: boasting of weaknesses); (c) God-directed glorying (VCG-03: Rom 5:2, vc=33874: boasting in hope of God's glory; Phili 3:3, vc=33879: glorying in Christ Jesus). This three-register semantic range is the most complex of any term in M08: the same verb covers all three moral evaluations depending on direction. Ha.lal similarly spans self-directed boasting (VCG-01) and God-directed praise (the set-aside M22 ha.lal verses that carry the praise register).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Fusioō operates across two primary semantic registers in the NT: (a) CHAR-4 register — cognitive self-inflation (1Cor 4:6; 4:18; 4:19; 5:2; 8:1; 13:4; Col 2:18 — M08-D-VCG-01); (b) No significant positive or divine-attribute register — unlike rum/ga.on (CHAR-1's vocabulary) or kauchaomai (CHAR-3's vocabulary), fusioō does not appear in a divine-majesty or approved-form register. The semantic range is narrower and more uniformly negative than CHAR-1's or CHAR-3's vocabulary: fusioō is consistently used for the condemned form of cognitive self-inflation, without the multi-register spanning of the other M08 vocabulary. This confirms CHAR-4 as the most lexically focused of the M08 characteristics.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Ga.on (H1347) in M08-CHAR-5 operates in the proud-might subset — a subset of its broader semantic range. Beyond CHAR-5, ga.on spans: (a) M22 divine majesty/exaltation (Exo 15:1 — "I will sing to the Lord, for he has triumphed gloriously [ga.on]" — set aside in Phase 5.5 as M22 content); (b) M23 legitimate national strength (set aside in Phase 5.5 — 122 M22-register verses including legitimate strength uses). The §3.D corpus retains only the proud-might subset where ga.on evidences strength misused as self-exaltation. Ma.rom similarly spans M22 (God's lofty dwelling — set aside) and M23 (fortified heights as legitimate military strategy) alongside the CHAR-5 register. The semantic range of the primary CHAR-5 terms is thus deliberately subset through the Phase 5.5 set-aside process.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The semantic range comparison reveals the cluster's most important cross-register vocabulary pattern (Observations #11 and #12). The g-'-h and r-w-m root families span M08 (CHAR-1, CHAR-5) and M22 (divine majesty/exaltation) — confirmed by the Phase 5.5 set-aside of 122 M22-register verses. The kauchaomai/ha.lal families span M08-CHAR-3 (self-directed boasting VCG-01) and M22 (God-directed glorying VCG-03). The ga.on, ma.rom, shal.le.tet families span M08-CHAR-5 and M23 (strength/power/dominion). The z-d family (CHAR-2) is distinctive to M08 within the programme evidence. The fusioō/tufoō/huperfroneō family (CHAR-4) is distinctive to M08's NT-primary cognitive register. The cluster-synthesis: M08's semantic range is comprehensively cross-register — the cluster's primary vocabulary spans M22 (through CHAR-1/CHAR-3/CHAR-5), M23 (through CHAR-5), and M09 (through the same-verse opposites in Jam 4:6; 1Pe 5:5; Pro 11:2).

**[CHAR-2]** E — Hupakoē/hupakouō across the corpus span: *theological-soteriological:* obedience of faith (Rom1:5; 16:26 — the culminating response to the gospel); *Christological:* Christ's obedience as redemptive act (Rom5:19; Heb5:8); *communal-relational:* household obedience (Eph6:1; Col3:20); *apostolic-communal:* sustained community obedience to teaching (Phili2:12; 2Th3:14); *eschatological:* the peoples' submission to the coming ruler (Gen49:10); *volitional-inner:* heart-located obedience as the inner disposition (Rom6:17). The semantic range is unusually broad — from the most intimate inner disposition to cosmic eschatological telos — confirming the characteristic's structural centrality.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Dak.ka's semantic range within this corpus: *state of being crushed in spirit* (Psa34:18 — the inward crushing that produces the brokenhearted condition); *character of the spirit that is contrite* (Isa57:15 — the spirit characterised by this crushing, paired with lowliness). The semantic range in this corpus is deliberately focused: the term describes the inner state of the crushed/broken spirit and its character before God. It does not span the full semantic field of the Hebrew root (which can include physical crushing); within M09 the term is being used specifically for the inner-being register of spirit-crushing in relation to moral failure and divine holiness.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Metriopatheō's semantic range in this corpus: *pastoral-mediating gentleness* toward the erring (Heb5:2 — dealing with the ignorant and wayward); this is the measured-compassionate-restraint register. Broader usage in Greek literature includes: measured emotional response that avoids both excessive passion and cold detachment (a Stoic virtue term). The term thus has both a general philosophical sense (emotional moderation) and a specifically relational-pastoral sense in Heb5:2 (compassionate measured dealing with the erring). Okneō's semantic range: hesitation, reluctance, slothful delay — in Act9:38 its absence is named as what is expected, so the semantic range is indirectly present as what the community expects not to find in Peter.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Semnotēs's semantic range across the three §3.D verses: *civic-public* (1Ti2:2 — the character quality enabling peaceful godly public life); *household-leadership* (1Ti3:4 — the inner gravity producing ordered household authority); *pedagogical* (Tit2:7 — the gravitas authenticating teaching). The full semantic range spans civic, familial, and pedagogical contexts — all three spheres of ordered human social existence. The range confirms the characteristic's comprehensive social-ordering function rather than its confinement to a single social sphere.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Na.div's semantic range in this corpus: *spontaneous inner generosity in worship-offering* (Exo35:5/22; 2Ch29:31 — free-will offering for tabernacle and temple); *wholehearted skilled service* (1Ch28:21 — willing man with skill for service); *spirit-level freely-given devotion after moral failure* (Psa51:12 — willing spirit as divine gift). The full range spans: corporate worship generosity, individual skilled service, and personal devotional orientation. The term thus operates across the communal, vocational, and personal registers — confirming it is a comprehensive characteristic rather than situationally confined.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The semantic range of the tapein- family and ka.na is broad. *Moral-relational:* the dominant register in this corpus — voluntary self-lowering before God (ka.na corpus); the character-disposition of the renewed person (tapeinofrosunē in Eph4:2; Phili2:3; Col3:12). *Social-circumstantial:* the humble estate of social lowness (tapeinōsis in Luk1:48; tapeinos in Luk1:52) — no explicit moral valuation but an objective social condition. *Creaturely-eschatological:* the lowly body (Phili3:21 tapeinōsis) — the creaturely condition of mortal embodiment. *Vocational:* Paul's ministry-humility (Act20:19 tapeinofrosunē) — sustained character in demanding contexts. The range spans social, moral, creaturely, and volitional registers — but the corpus concentrates in the moral-relational register.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The semantic ranges reveal each characteristic's breadth of application and confirm the cluster's phenomenological diversity. Humility (CHAR-1): widest range — moral-relational (dominant), social-circumstantial (lowly estate — Luk1:48), creaturely-eschatological (lowly body — Phili3:21), vocational (ministry context — Act20:19). Submission (CHAR-2): next widest — theological-soteriological (obedience of faith), Christological (Christ's obedience), communal-relational (household), apostolic-communal, eschatological (peoples' submission — Gen49:10), volitional-inner (heart-located disposition — Rom6:17). Contrition (CHAR-3): deliberately narrow — the state of being crushed in spirit before God (both verses in the same register). Meekness and Gentleness (CHAR-4): two registers (pastoral-mediating gentleness — Heb5:2; non-hesitating volitional readiness — Act9:38). findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the vocabulary makes all three distinctions explicitly:

**Disposition vs. act:** H5546 (sal.lach — adjective, disposition) vs. H5545 (sa.lach — verb, act). The vocabulary distinguishes between God as constitutively forgiving (disposition) and God performing the specific act of forgiving (act). The Greek does not have a separate dispositional adjective — the disposition is carried by the noun and participial forms.

**Received vs. given:** G0863H appears in both passive and active forms. The passive ("your sins are forgiven" — perfect passive, Luk 7:47) names the received state; the active imperative ("forgive your brother" — Mat 18:35) names the given act. The same term grammatically marks both directions.

**Condition vs. quality:** G0859 (afesis — the condition of release, the state of being forgiven) vs. H5547 (se.li.chah — the abstract quality/possession of forgiveness as a divine attribute). The noun forms distinguish the human condition produced (afesis) from the divine quality possessed (se.li.chah).

The vocabulary is therefore **structurally differentiated** — it has distinct forms for each of the major analytical categories needed to describe forgiveness in its full inner-being complexity.

Most characteristics name only the quality, not the condition of its proper object.

The dual primary anchor finding (Hos 11:8 for divine compassion at constitutional depth; Luke 10:33 for human compassion as moral norm) establishes the two poles of the characteristic's evidential range. Three key argument structures: compassion-mission logic (Matt 9:36-10:1 — compassion as the theological engine of missional response), divine compassion-repentance ground (Joel 2:13 — divine character as the ground of human response-posture), Good Samaritan's moral logic (Luke 10:25-37 — compassion as the answer to "who is my neighbour?"). Three human science frameworks illuminate the vocabulary with genuine alignment (affective neuroscience, virtue ethics, attachment theory) and all three diverge from the biblical account at specific points (sovereignty vs automaticity; cross-boundary extension exceeding natural empathic scope; purposive suffering in Jas 5:11 requiring teleological frame). The LXX systematic analysis gap (NO_WORD_ANALYSIS flag on 98 terms) is the most significant methodological limitation — a new gap for the programme.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-007: T7 produces three analytically distinctive findings. First, the vocabulary is structurally complete: every dimension of grace's operation has a corresponding term — disposition (chen, charis as noun),…
findings.finding_value: T7 produces three analytically distinctive findings. First, the vocabulary is structurally complete: every dimension of grace's operation has a corresponding term — disposition (chen, charis as noun), act (chanan, charizō), completed state (charitoō — G5487, NT coinage), receiving-side posture (tachanum, techinah), structural negative (acharistos — built from the same root with alpha-privative). No other characteristic in the review set has equivalent lexical completeness. Second, the NT coinage (charitoō, G5487) is analytically significant: coined because existing vocabulary was insufficient to name "standing-in-favour as a completed, continuing state." The perfect passive kecharitōmenē (Luk 1:28) encodes completed act with continuing state — a grammatical form that no prior vocabulary could carry. Third, the human-science/Scripture divergence is the most significant methodological finding in the review set: at the point of constitutional incapacity (the person cannot respond to grace without grace — SD026, SD008), every human science framework diverges from the biblical account. Affective neuroscience, virtue ethics, and cultural anthropology all assume the person has some prior capacity for response; the biblical account denies this at the point of maximum need (the constitutionally dead of Eph 2:1-5). The LXX analysis gap (T7.1 P8) is confirmed as a methodological limitation.

The spirit-reception level (T2.1) is carried by the perfect passive form of charitoō (kecharitōmenē — the completed act of being-made-the-object-of-grace, with continuing state) — the most precise grammatical encoding of a constitutional arrival that has permanently changed the person's standing. findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-068-025: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-le…
findings.finding_value: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-level finding. T7.1 confirms: the chen root family embeds both the giving side (chen — favour, chanan — to be gracious) and the receiving-seeking side (tachanum, techinah — supplication) in a single etymological family. This is unique in the programme's vocabulary data: no other characteristic has the giving-side and receiving-side vocabulary built from the same root. T4's relational architecture and T7's lexical analysis are the relational and lexical descriptions of the same structural reality — that grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit whose two sides are inseparable at the root level.

findings.finding_value: T6's structural uniqueness (grace is not produced by any inner-being characteristic — categorically the originating point of the causal chain) and T7's vocabulary structural completeness (every dimension of grace's operation has a corresponding term, including the structural negative acharistos) confirm and explain each other. T6 establishes that grace stands outside the characteristic-production network; T7 establishes that the vocabulary encodes this structural position with unique completeness — including the negative (acharistos) and the NT coinage (charitoō) as markers of grace's conceptual uniqueness. The shared anchor verses (T6.6) are also T7's most evidentially rich texts: Eph 2:8 (which anchors multiple co-occurring registries) carries the most complete single-verse expression of grace's structural position (sovereign gift, not of works, producing faith). T6 and T7 mutually confirm that grace's structural uniqueness in the programme landscape corresponds to a lexical uniqueness in the vocabulary — both point to the same underlying analytical claim: grace is categorically distinct from every other inner-being characteristic.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-099-007: T7 reveals that the evidential foundation for kindness is now strong following cross-registry supplementation, but with a residual gap at the LXX/semantic-history level. The primary lexical finding: c…
findings.finding_value: T7 reveals that the evidential foundation for kindness is now strong following cross-registry supplementation, but with a residual gap at the LXX/semantic-history level. The primary lexical finding: chesed's semantic range (goodness/kindness/faithfulness as a single integrated concept) does not map onto English "kindness" without loss — every English translation must choose between the loyalty dimension and the warmth dimension of chesed; neither alone captures the whole. This translation complexity is not a peripheral philological problem but a structural one for understanding what kindness is — if you translate chesed as "love" (as many English Bibles do), you lose the specifically loyal-relational character; if you translate it as "kindness," you lose the covenant-faithfulness dimension. The LXX gap (chesed → eleos/mercy) is analytically significant: the Greek-speaking world's reception of the Hebrew chesed concept emphasised its compassion/mercy dimension over its faithfulness dimension — which may partly explain why chrēstos/chrēstotēs in the NT emphasises benign goodness over covenantal loyalty. The primary anchor verse finding is secure: Lam 3:22 is the structural foundation — it asserts what no other verse asserts: that divine kindness is unconditional in its permanence even when everything else has failed. The most useful human science framework is developmental psychology (attachment theory illuminating the chesed relationship as secure-base attachment), but the biblical chesed exceeds it in covenantal obligation and moral transformation. T7's most significant intra-tier finding: the translation complexity of chesed is not merely a translation problem but a definitional one — the programme's use of "kindness" as the registry name captures only part of what chesed names; the full concept requires "loyal kindness" or "covenant faithfulness" as a corrective.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-013: T1's working definition of kindness and T7's lexical foundation finding are in direct productive tension. T7 reveals that the Hebrew chesed cannot be translated as "kindness" without loss of its faith…
findings.finding_value: T1's working definition of kindness and T7's lexical foundation finding are in direct productive tension. T7 reveals that the Hebrew chesed cannot be translated as "kindness" without loss of its faithfulness/loyalty dimension — every English rendering is reductive. T1's working definition ("stable inner disposition of loyal goodwill") attempts to bridge this gap by combining both dimensions, but T7's finding that chesed's semantic range spans goodness/kindness/faithfulness as a single unified concept means that the programme's registry name ("kindness") is itself a definitional understatement. This tension is analytically productive: it means that Session C's prose on "what kindness is" must grapple with a characteristic whose Hebrew name is richer than its English label, and that every claim made about kindness in the programme should be held against the chesed evidence where the fuller concept is preserved. T7's finding about chrēstologia as a possible NT coinage also illuminates T1: if chrēstologia was coined precisely to name the pathology of pleasant speech without inner disposition, then the Greek-speaking community around Paul had a clear concept of kindness-as-disposition whose counterfeit needed a specific name — confirming T1's finding that the distinction between genuine and counterfeit kindness was analytically important to the early church.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-018: T2's constitutional location findings (heart as primary site; no body deposit; Spirit as origin) are grounded in and confirmed by T7's lexical evidence. The explicit heart-inscription language of Pro …
findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional location findings (heart as primary site; no body deposit; Spirit as origin) are grounded in and confirmed by T7's lexical evidence. The explicit heart-inscription language of Pro 3:3 — the most important T2 finding — is a direct chesed text: the term being inscribed is chesed itself. T7's finding about chesed's semantic range (goodness/kindness/faithfulness as a unified concept) reinforces T2's origin finding: the triple origin structure (divine → Spirit → formed) is exactly what the chesed vocabulary expects — it names God's own inner attribute (Exo 34:6 — abounding in steadfast love), which the Spirit reproduces in the believer, which is then formed through practice and encounter. The T7 LXX finding (chesed → eleos/mercy) has a constitutional implication: the LXX translation emphasises the compassion/affective dimension of chesed over its faithfulness/constitutional dimension — which may explain why the NT Greek kindness vocabulary (chrēstos/chrēstotēs) emphasises quality of character rather than covenant obligation. The two tiers together: lexical depth (T7) explains why constitutional location (T2) lands at the heart — chesed is precisely a heart-level characteristic because it names the covenantal faithfulness that is inscribed in the inner person.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-025: T4's finding that the divine-to-human direction is the most extensively evidenced direction in the registry is directly confirmed by T7's lexical finding: H2617A (chesed) group 536-001 (180 relevant v…
findings.finding_value: T4's finding that the divine-to-human direction is the most extensively evidenced direction in the registry is directly confirmed by T7's lexical finding: H2617A (chesed) group 536-001 (180 relevant verses, dominant subject GOD) is the largest single data group in the entire cross-registry material. The quantity of evidence for divine kindness toward humans is not an analytical artefact — it is a lexical and textual reality. T7's LXX finding (chesed → eleos/mercy) is relevant to T4's human-to-God direction: the LXX's emphasis on the mercy/compassion dimension over the faithfulness dimension may have shaped how the human-to-God movement was perceived in the Greek-speaking community — as appeal to divine mercy rather than appeal to divine faithfulness. The T7 primary anchor verse finding (Lam 3:22) is the definitive statement of the T4 divine-to-human direction in its fullest form: the anchor verse is chosen precisely because it asserts the T4 interface's stability (never ceasing, always available) under maximum relational pressure (Jerusalem destroyed, T4 interface apparently withdrawn). The two tiers together confirm that the divine-to-human relational interface is both the most evidenced and the most definitionally important direction for kindness.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-027: T5's formation findings are directly grounded in T7's lexical evidence in a specific way: the three formation mechanisms (Spirit-formation, inscription, encounter) each correspond to a specific textua…
findings.finding_value: T5's formation findings are directly grounded in T7's lexical evidence in a specific way: the three formation mechanisms (Spirit-formation, inscription, encounter) each correspond to a specific textual cluster in the chesed corpus. Spirit-formation is the NT Greek evidence (Gal 5:22 — chrēstotēs as fruit of the Spirit); inscription is Pro 3:3 (chesed written on the heart — the clearest constitutional formation text); encounter is the Psalms lament/praise corpus (the psalmist encountering God's chesed in distress and being transformed). T7's literary finding that kindness appears across all major literary forms (lament, praise, narrative, instruction, argument) is the T5 formation diversity mapped onto literary genre — the formation occurs in all contexts and genres, not only in instructional texts. T7's most useful human science framework (developmental psychology / attachment theory) illuminates T5's formation arc: the chasid formation trajectory maps onto attachment theory's "secure attachment → exploration → resilience" pattern — the person who has received divine chesed as secure attachment base (Psa 23:4) is equipped to explore and sustain relational kindness toward others (T4 giving) and to withstand suffering without losing kindness (T5 suffering finding).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-099-028: T6's structural relationship findings and T7's lexical and literary findings are mutually confirming at the level of the semantic root. The T6 finding that the CHESED root family covers noun (chesed),…
findings.finding_value: T6's structural relationship findings and T7's lexical and literary findings are mutually confirming at the level of the semantic root. The T6 finding that the CHESED root family covers noun (chesed), verb (chasad), person (chasid), shame-negative (H2617B), and proper noun (Chesed) is a T7 lexical observation that has structural significance: a root family that spans all these categories is not merely a lexical curiosity but evidence that kindness (as the CHESED root names it) is a comprehensive inner-being reality — it has a noun form (what it is), a verb form (what it does), a person form (who embodies it), a consequence form (what happens when it fails), and a proper-noun instantiation (when it names a person). The T6 co-occurrence finding that kindness clusters with faithfulness, justice, and compassion maps directly onto the T7 semantic range finding that chesed itself encompasses goodness/kindness/faithfulness — the co-occurrence cluster is partly a reflection of the internal semantic complexity of chesed: different registries are studying different dimensions of what is, in the original Hebrew, a single concept. T7's primary anchor verse (Lam 3:22) is T6's most significant causal statement: the inexhaustibility of chesed (T7) is the precondition for the causal chain's stability (T6) — if chesed could run out, the chain would break.

findings.finding_value: T7 as a whole reveals the evidential and methodological shape of this registry's analysis. The vocabulary arc (Q&A-179) is the governing finding: two poles — na.tan (enacted) and emunah/hesed/pistis (constituted) — are both necessary and neither alone is sufficient. The grammatical gap (verb vs. nominal) maps directly onto the analytical distinction between the two poles. The literary diversity of the anchor corpus (narrative, prophecy, wisdom, liturgy) means no single interpretive lens covers the full evidence base. The primary analytical anchor (Hos 11:8) is identified for its unique revelation of the divine inner-being decision structure. The human science frameworks (virtue ethics, attachment theory) illuminate the characteristic while also diverging at critical points — the divergences are themselves analytically productive: biblical faithfulness requires both a virtue-ethical foundation (the character basis of giving) and something that virtue ethics cannot supply (the constitutive primacy of received divine giving as the ground of human virtue). What T7 reveals as a whole: the evidential base of this characteristic is rich, methodologically complex, and internally consistent. The two main methodological challenges — the registry label/OWNER term gap, and the legacy-VC status of all classified verses — are acknowledged and do not undermine the analysis but do qualify its certainty.

**[CLUSTER]** E. Yes — the vocabulary makes several significant distinctions:
- **State vs. act:** tsad.diq (the righteous person — state) vs. tsa.deq (to justify — act); dikaios (righteous — state/quality) vs. dikaioō (to justify — act). The Hebrew and Greek both distinguish the state of being righteous from the act of declaring or making righteous.
- **Condition vs. quality:** tse.da.qah (righteousness as quality, something the person possesses) vs. tse.deq (righteousness as standard, the norm against which the person is measured). Both are nouns from the same root but carry different emphases — the condition of the person vs. the external standard.
- **Disposition vs. act:** yo.sher/me.shar (uprightness as inner disposition) vs. tse.da.qah in its acted sense (righteous acts, expressed righteousness). The B-vocabulary specifically captures the dispositional dimension that the A-vocabulary covers more broadly.
- **Received vs. exercised:** dikaiōsis (the act of justification as received — the event of being declared righteous) vs. dikaiōma (the righteous acts of the saints — the expressed righteous living). The Greek distinguishes what is received (C: justification as event) from what is exercised (A2: righteous acts as evidence).

The verb/adjective/noun distinction in M15-A captures wisdom as character-quality (adj), as exercised act (verb), and as attribute possessed (noun) — three distinct aspects of the same characteristic.

(3) Provocation-dynamic vs anger-state: *ka.as* (H3707, to provoke to anger) names the provocation act; *orgē* names the resulting state. The vocabulary distinguishes: (1) Condition versus act: ya.gon/tu.gah (condition — sorrow in the heart) versus ba.khah (act — weeping); perilupos (condition — deeply sorrowful) versus klaiō (act — to weep). (2) Inner versus somatic: ya.gon (inner condition) versus dim.ah (somatic substance — tears). (4) Acute versus chronic: sunochē (acute anguish, constriction) versus ya.gon (chronic sorrow, lodged in the heart). The vocabulary's distinctions confirm the cluster's structural complexity — it is not one phenomenon described by synonyms but a family of related but distinct inner-being states.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes: (1) **gil** (act/condition — both forms) vs. **re.na.nah** (the sonic expression of exultation — the outward form); (2) **su.s** (the more volitional-affective, directed form) vs. **cha.dah** (the more responsive form — used for Jethro's spontaneous rejoicing); (3) nominal **gil** (H1524A — the exultation as a state: Psa 43:4 "God my exceeding joy"; Psa 45:15 "with joy and gladness") vs. verbal **gil** (H1523 — the exultation as an act). These distinctions allow the vocabulary to capture both the spontaneous and the cultivated, both the inner state and the outward expression of exultation.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes: (1) **sa.mach** (act) vs. **sim.chah** (state) vs. **sa.me.ach** (character) — grammatical distinctions between the event, the condition, and the person; (2) **sa.mach** (general Joy-act) vs. **agalliao** (intensified exultant Joy) vs. **sunchairo** (co-Joy) — the Greek terms distinguish degree of intensity and whether the Joy is solitary or shared; (3) **chairo** (act) vs. **chara** (state) — NT parallel of the OT sa.mach/sim.chah distinction; (4) **sa.s.von** (restoration-Joy, forward-oriented) vs. **sa.mach** (present Joy) — distinct sub-registers of the OT joy vocabulary.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Yes: (1) **agalliao** (verbal — the act of exulting) vs. **agalliasis** (nominal — the state of exultation or the quality of gladness as anointing); (2) **ba.lag** (fragile-attempted cheerfulness) vs. **agalliao** (Spirit-enabled intense exultation) — the two terms together name the full spectrum of Suffering-Joy from its fragile minimum to its Spirit-enabled maximum; (3) **mav.li.git** (comfort as desired but absent) vs. **agalliao** (joy present despite adversity) — the two terms frame Suffering-Joy's structural opposite (comfort-gone) against its fullest positive form.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes: (1) **tov** (predicative — quality/condition) vs. **tov-min** (comparative — surpassing worth); (2) **lo-tov** (negated tov — moral deficiency and its condemnation: Exo 18:17; Neh 5:9; Pro 17:26 etc.) — the structural-opposite form built into the primary term; (3) **tov-lev** (compound: good-of-heart — Est 5:9's "glad of heart" — M04-B-VCG-04, cross-assigned to Gladness's relational-personal register: the inner-being compound confirming heart-location of circumstantial gladness); (4) **makarismos** (G3108 — the NT blessedness form, distinguishing declarative-status-gladness from experiential-circumstantial gladness).

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes, across the full vocabulary: (1) **sha.a.shu.im** — the treasuring-cherishing aspect (multi-faceted, accumulated pleasure); **sha.a** — the playful-carefree aspect; **a.nog** — the luxuriating-resting aspect; **o.neg** — the noun of that luxuriating quality; these four together distinguish the affective-register's nuances; (2) **cha.phets** (verb) vs. **che.phets** (noun) vs. **cha.phets** (adj) — distinguish the act, the condition, and the disposition of volitional Delight; (3) **sunēdomai** — the solidarity-Delight aspect (delighting together with, in inner-being); (4) **arestos** — the acceptability/pleasing-compliance aspect; (5) **ni.cho.ach** — the soothing-aroma aspect (the quality of what rises from correct worship); (6) **ta.a.nug** — the daintiness/tender-parental aspect; (7) **che.med** — the covetous-lustful aspect of corrupt Delight; (8) **a.li.tsut** — the predatory-exultation aspect of corrupt Delight.

**[CHAR-5]** E — Yes: (1) **na.im/na.em/no.am** — the relational-aesthetic pleasantness of persons, wisdom, and God's character; (2) **ni.cho.ach** — the worship-specific soothing-Pleasure at the divine-human worship interface; (3) **a.nog/ta.a.nug/ed.nah** — the luxury-sensory Pleasure of pampered ease and material comfort; (4) **a.las** — the exultant pleasure-delight at what one enjoys (distinct from the gentler na.em); (5) **tov better-than** — the wisdom-comparative moral-calibration of Pleasure. Together the terms distinguish five distinct aspects: relational-aesthetic (na.em), worship-receptive (ni.cho.ach), luxury-sensory (a.nog), exultant-pleasure (a.las), and wisdom-calibrated (tov).

**[CHAR-6]** E — Yes: (1) **pa.la (verb)** — the active doing and passive experiencing of wonder; (2) **pe.le (noun)** — wonder as a substantive quality/reality; (3) **miph.la.ah** — the wondrous work as an object; (4) **thambeō** — the seizure-quality of sudden wonder-astonishment; (5) **thaumazō** — the sustained marvelling state; (6) **thauma** — wonder as a substantive noun (2Cor 11:14's "no wonder"). Together the terms distinguish: the act of doing/experiencing wonder (pa.la verbal), the quality of being wonderful (pe.le nominal), the object that produces wonder (miph.la.ah), the moment of seizure (thambeō), and the sustained state (thaumazō).

**[CLUSTER]** E — All seven characteristics have internally differentiated vocabularies that distinguish distinct aspects of the characteristic. The most analytically significant comparative finding: **Delight (Char 4) has the most internally differentiated vocabulary** of any M04 characteristic — sha.a.shu.im (cherishing-resting), sha.a (carefree playfulness), a.nog (luxuriating ease), cha.phets (volitional direction), arestos (obedience-acceptability), ni.cho.ach (soothing-aroma), ta.a.nug (parental tenderness), che.med (covetous-corrupt), and a.li.tsut (predatory-corrupt) together span from the most tender (sha.a — playful, carefree) through the most volitionally-charged (cha.phets) to the most corrupt (a.li.tsut). **Suffering-Joy (Char 7) has the most diagnostically contrasted vocabulary** — ba.lag (fragile, barely-attainable) vs. agalliao (Spirit-enabled intense) are the sharpest internal vocabulary contrast in the cluster, marking the full range from the characteristic's minimum to its maximum.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The distinction between *bosh* (the felt experience of shame — more subjective, inner) and *ke.lim.mah* (the disgrace as witnessed and socially visible — more objective, outward) maps onto a genuine inner-outer distinction within CHAR-1. *Cha.pher* (disappointed, confounded) carries the cognitive-collapse dimension (the failing of a confident expectation). *Bu.shah* (shame as covering, enveloping condition) captures the sustained-burden dimension. *Aischunē* names the condition; *aischunō* the verbal action of being ashamed; *kataischunō* the thoroughly-shamed state. The vocabulary thus distinguishes inner subjective experience, social visibility, cognitive collapse, chronic burden, and the act vs. condition of shame.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Ka.lam operates primarily as a verb (being humiliated). Sha.phel operates as verb (Hiphil — causing to be brought low) and adjective (sha.phel nefesh — lowly of spirit). The verbal dominance confirms CHAR-2's action-character: it is something done, not merely something possessed. Semantic range covers bodily-social, national-political, and cosmic dimensions (moon and sun ashamed, Isa 24:23) — CHAR-2 applies wherever pride-structures or elevated standing exists.

---

**[CHAR-3]** E — Primary terms: Atimazō (G0818): to dishonour, treat as without honour — active verb, the dishonoring act. Atimia (G0819): dishonour as a state — the condition of assigned or received diminished worth. Entrepō (G1788) in its absence register: the failure of the regard-faculty. Paradeigmatizō (G3856): to expose publicly, hold up to contempt. Roots: a-timē — without honour, without worth — the alpha-privative of honour. Structural opposite: timaō (to honour, to assign worth) and timē (honour as assigned worth-recognition). The evidence pairs these explicitly in Joh 8:49. The CHAR-3 corpus is entirely NT — the OT vocabulary for relational worth-denial (qa.lah, H7034; entrepō in its absence register) is thinner. The NT's christological context gives CHAR-3 its sharpest definition: dishonour as what is directed at Jesus personally and at God through human hypocrisy. Person-type: the "unjust judge" (Luk 18:2) is the closest person-type but is not a technical term. Supplication: the widow's persistent coming to the judge (Luk 18:3) is a supplication for the reversal of CHAR-3 — the only supplication-context in the corpus.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — Aischros is consistently adjectival — it modifies conduct, gain, or situations. Aschēmosunē is consistently nominal — naming the quality. The adjectival/nominal dominance confirms CHAR-4's quality-character: it is about the property of things (shameful conduct, indecent acts) rather than the experience of persons. The semantic range is limited: all primary CHAR-4 terms specifically name the quality of moral shamefulness — they do not range into the social-status register of the shame vocabulary.

---

**[CHAR-5]** E — Exoutheneō operates as a verb (to despise, to treat as nothing). Atimazō operates as a verb (to dishonour, to treat shamefully). Loidoria is a noun (reviling, verbal abuse). The verbal dominance confirms CHAR-5's action-character: the contempt is always something done — an active verbal or physical or attitudinal act. The semantic range spans inner attitude (VCG-01 — the exoutheneō of the self-righteous), physical violence (VCG-02 — the atimazō of violent treatment), and verbal assault (VCG-03 — the loidoria of reputation-attack).

---

**[CHAR-6]** E — Both terms function primarily as nouns naming a condition: "in the innocence of my hands" (Gen 20:5; Psa 26:6) — the innocence is a quality of the hands named nominally. The nominal form confirms CHAR-6's quality-character: innocence is a condition the person possesses (or fails to possess), not a direction or act. The semantic range of niq.qa.von is narrow within this corpus: it specifically names the moral cleanness that enables approach to God and protects against guilt-shame. It does not range into the social-status vocabulary of shame's other terms.

---

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's primary vocabulary is distributed across three grammatical categories: stative verbs (bosh — being ashamed; sha.phel — being brought low) name the experienced conditions (Chars 1, 2); transitive verbs (atimazō — to dishonour; exoutheneō — to despise) name the enacted acts (Chars 3, 5); adjectives/nouns (aischros — shameful; niq.qa.von — innocence; atimia — dishonour as a noun) name the evaluative quality and its counter (Chars 4, 6). This grammatical distribution mirrors the cluster's characteristic diversity: conditions are expressed statically, enacted acts transitively, and qualities adjectivally/nominally. Semantic range: from the acute personal shame of the psalmist (bosh in Psa 44:15) to the cosmic shame of the moon and sun before divine glory (bosh in Isa 24:23), and from the intimate hand-washing innocence (niq.qa.von in Psa 26:6) to the incapacity-for-innocence of an entire people (niq.qa.von in Hos 8:5). M07 applies its vocabulary at every level of human existence.

Pro 16:5 (vc=12083, M08-A1-VCG-03) — "arrogant in heart" (ga.vo.ah) — dispositional; Dan 11:36 (vc=34235, M08-A1-VCG-02) — "he shall exalt himself" (rum verb active) — act. Person-type versus quality: ge.eh (H1343) — the proud person as a type (Job 40:11, vc=33949: "look on everyone who is proud/ge.eh"); ga.on, ga.a.vah — the quality of pride itself. The vocabulary is grammatically differentiated to address CHAR-1 across its full range of manifestation.

The graduated register: M08-B-VCG-01 (zid — the acute boiling-over act), M08-B-VCG-02 (za.don/zed — the habitual insolence quality and person-type), M08-B-VCG-03 (authadēs, tolmētēs, archō — NT precision terms for self-will and reckless boldness). The vocabulary distinguishes CHAR-2 as act (zid), quality (za.don), and person-type (zed) — the same three-level structure evidenced in CHAR-1 but through different terms.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes. Disposition vs act: alazoneia (inner boasting disposition) vs kauchaomai (the verbal/social act of boasting). Person-type: alazōn (the braggart — a stable social identity type — 2Ti 3:2, vc=33868; Rom 1:30, vc=33867). Second axis — agent vs condition: Characteristics 1-3 use vocabulary that names the person's condition (ta.me adj — the person is unclean); Characteristic 4 uses vocabulary that names the agent's character (akathartos — the spirit is unclean). This is the cluster's most analytically significant vocabulary distinction: in three of four characteristics, the vocabulary describes the condition of the person; in the fourth, the vocabulary describes the character of the external agent who produces the condition. The vocabulary thus encodes the cluster's fundamental structural division: conditions arising from within or through the person (Chars 1-3) vs a condition imposed from without by an alien agency (Char 4).

findings.session_b_note:
Yes — the vocabulary includes multiple terms for the opposite or absence, operating at different levels:

**The judicial-prohibition vocabulary (chus in negative):** "Your eye shall not pity (chus)" is the most direct verbal naming of compassion's absence — or more precisely, its deliberate suppression. This is not merely the absence of compassion but the active overriding of it.

**H2617B chesed as shame (negative semantic pole):** The CHASAD root includes H2617B as the negative pole — shame/disgrace. The same root that names steadfast love also names the condition that is its opposite: relational exposure and violation. This is the most structurally interesting "opposite" term in the data — it is embedded within the compassion vocabulary itself, not in a separate antonym.

**G1652 eleeinos (pitiable — condition requiring compassion):** This names not the opposite of compassion but the state that exists in its absence — the pitiable condition of the person who has not received compassion. It is the absence-marker on the receiving side rather than the giving side.

**Implied hardness:** The judicial-prohibition contexts imply a named absence on the character side — the hard heart, the closed eye. While not a single term, the phrase "your eye shall not pity" functions as the inverse character statement: the person who does not pity, whose eye is closed to need.

findings.finding_value: Love's evidential foundation is the most comprehensive in the programme. The primary terms (chesed, agapē/agapaō, racham/rachamim, ahavah, dod, phileō) cover the full constitutional range: willed-covenantal (chesed), Spirit-produced self-giving (agapē), somatic-compassionate (racham), intense-erotic (ahavah/dod), and naturally affective (phileō). The semantic range of the primary terms spans from divine ontology (God is love) to moral inversion (love of darkness) — the widest semantic arc in the programme. The primary anchor is Lam 3:22 — love's most definitive affirmation precisely at the moment of maximum empirical falsification: a theological confession rather than an empirical observation. The LXX connection is partially evidenced (agapē as chesed-translated); full LXX analysis is limited by NO_WORD_ANALYSIS flags. The human science frameworks identified (attachment theory, virtue ethics) are named as Session D pointers but not elaborated — the instruction prohibits importing framework content not grounded in the data.

The full vocabulary arc (from womb — most intimate — to almsgiving — most institutional) is unique in the programme: no other characteristic traverses this complete arc with equivalent lexical clarity. Three key argument structures: compassion-mission logic (Matt 9:36-10:1 — compassion as the theological engine of missional response), divine compassion-repentance ground (Joel 2:13 — divine character as the ground of human response-posture), Good Samaritan's moral logic (Luke 10:25-37 — compassion as the answer to "who is my neighbour?"). Three human science frameworks illuminate the vocabulary with genuine alignment (affective neuroscience, virtue ethics, attachment theory) and all three diverge from the biblical account at specific points (sovereignty vs automaticity; cross-boundary extension exceeding natural empathic scope; purposive suffering in Jas 5:11 requiring teleological frame). The CHASAD root crossing two clusters (T6.4 — most unexpected structural finding) is confirmed and extended by T7's vocabulary analysis: the CHASAD root includes shame as the negative semantic pole embedded within the root itself (T7.1 P5), not as an external antonym. Exod 34:6 as the programme's most multiply-anchored verse (T6.6 — 6 registries) is also T7's most evidentially rich single text — the verse that carries the most structural connections is the same verse that is most analytically central to the vocabulary analysis. The love co-occurrence dominance (T6.1 — 196/351 verses) is confirmed by T7's vocabulary arc: the vocabulary's fullest range (womb to almsgiving) overlaps extensively with the love vocabulary's range, which is why they co-occur across more than half of all active verses.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-068-007: T7 produces three analytically distinctive findings. First, the vocabulary is structurally complete: every dimension of grace's operation has a corresponding term — disposition (chen, charis as noun),…
findings.finding_value: T7 produces three analytically distinctive findings. First, the vocabulary is structurally complete: every dimension of grace's operation has a corresponding term — disposition (chen, charis as noun), act (chanan, charizō), completed state (charitoō — G5487, NT coinage), receiving-side posture (tachanum, techinah), structural negative (acharistos — built from the same root with alpha-privative). No other characteristic in the review set has equivalent lexical completeness. Second, the NT coinage (charitoō, G5487) is analytically significant: coined because existing vocabulary was insufficient to name "standing-in-favour as a completed, continuing state." The perfect passive kecharitōmenē (Luk 1:28) encodes completed act with continuing state — a grammatical form that no prior vocabulary could carry. Third, the human-science/Scripture divergence is the most significant methodological finding in the review set: at the point of constitutional incapacity (the person cannot respond to grace without grace — SD026, SD008), every human science framework diverges from the biblical account. Affective neuroscience, virtue ethics, and cultural anthropology all assume the person has some prior capacity for response; the biblical account denies this at the point of maximum need (the constitutionally dead of Eph 2:1-5). The LXX analysis gap (T7.1 P8) is confirmed as a methodological limitation.

The act kind (chanan, charizō) has dedicated verbal forms. The completed-state kind (charitoō — NT coinage, G5487) required a new word because existing vocabulary could not carry the concept of standing-in-favour as a completed, continuing state. The character-quality kind (chen in conduct and speech — 889-003) is carried by chen's adjectival and behavioural register. The vocabulary is structurally complete for the four kinds — each kind has a corresponding lexical form. T7's NT coinage finding (charitoō) is the lexical evidence that T1's four-kind analysis is correct: the fourth kind (standing as completed state) required new vocabulary because it was conceptually unique.

findings.finding_value: T2's constitutional levels are carried by specific grammatical forms in T7. The spirit-reception level (T2.1) is carried by the perfect passive form of charitoō (kecharitōmenē — the completed act of being-made-the-object-of-grace, with continuing state) — the most precise grammatical encoding of a constitutional arrival that has permanently changed the person's standing. The soul-standing level (T2.2) is carried by charis as noun (the inhabited state of favour) and chen as the relational standing-in-favour term. The character-expression level is carried by chen in its conduct/speech register (889-003) and charizō in its human-forgiving mode. T7's NT coinage finding (charitoō invented to carry the standing-in-favour concept) is the lexical evidence that T2's spirit-level reception was conceptually unprecedented — no prior vocabulary could name what happened constitutionally when grace-as-standing arrived.

findings.finding_value: T4's most analytically distinctive finding (the vocabulary encodes the two-sided grace-circuit in a single root: chen/chanan for giving; tachanum/techinah for seeking) is T7's most significant root-level finding. T7.1 confirms: the chen root family embeds both the giving side (chen — favour, chanan — to be gracious) and the receiving-seeking side (tachanum, techinah — supplication) in a single etymological family. This is unique in the programme's vocabulary data: no other characteristic has the giving-side and receiving-side vocabulary built from the same root. T4's relational architecture and T7's lexical analysis are the relational and lexical descriptions of the same structural reality — that grace is constitutively a two-sided circuit whose two sides are inseparable at the root level.

findings.finding_value: T6's structural uniqueness (grace is not produced by any inner-being characteristic — categorically the originating point of the causal chain) and T7's vocabulary structural completeness (every dimension of grace's operation has a corresponding term, including the structural negative acharistos) confirm and explain each other. T6 establishes that grace stands outside the characteristic-production network; T7 establishes that the vocabulary encodes this structural position with unique completeness — including the negative (acharistos) and the NT coinage (charitoō) as markers of grace's conceptual uniqueness. The shared anchor verses (T6.6) are also T7's most evidentially rich texts: Eph 2:8 (which anchors multiple co-occurring registries) carries the most complete single-verse expression of grace's structural position (sovereign gift, not of works, producing faith). T6 and T7 mutually confirm that grace's structural uniqueness in the programme landscape corresponds to a lexical uniqueness in the vocabulary — both point to the same underlying analytical claim: grace is categorically distinct from every other inner-being characteristic.

findings.finding_value: The M01 vocabulary does not include a dedicated antonym term. The structural opposites are expressed through: (1) **negative constructions** — "no fear of God before their eyes" (Psa 36:1; Rom 3:18); "do not fear" (the entire M01-B-VCG-06 corpus); "not afraid" (numerous instances); (2) **paired contrasting terms** — cha.tat in M01-D (dismay/shattering) is used in M01-D-VCG-04 as the opposite of composure and courage; (3) **positive opposites** — the vocabulary of trust (batach) and faith (emunah) function as the structural opposites of fear in multiple passages but are not M01 cluster terms. The absence of a dedicated antonym for reverential fear (other than through negative construction) is consistent with Hebrew vocabulary structure: the positive disposition is the norm, and its absence is expressed as negation rather than through a competing positive term.

M01-G does have a specified positive opposite within the text: the spirit of power, love, and self-control (2Ti 1:7 anchor) is explicitly named as the opposite of timidity. The term deilia's opposite is implicitly andreia (courage) in the Greek ethical tradition, though this term does not appear in the M01 verse evidence.

The cluster lacks a dedicated antonym vocabulary. The absence is expressed through negation ("no fear," "not afraid"), through commanded-against states ("do not fear"), and through named positive alternatives (trust, faith, love). This pattern is consistent with a characteristic whose primary expression is positive (the reverential orientation) and whose absence is expressed as a diagnostic failure rather than an achieved counter-state.

The Greek *eirēnē* (peace) as the opposite of quarrelsome strife (M02-F) is implied in M02-F-VCG-02 (Pro 17:1 — "even abundance with strife is worse than a dry crust with peace"). The structural opposite is not a dedicated anger-opposite term but a family of relenting/turning/peace terms that name the anger's absence or resolution.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes, by negation and antithesis within the corpus. The VCG-02 passages use the same terms (gil, su.s, re.na.nah) negated or inverted: Job 3:6–7 (night wished to be barren of re.na.nah); Joe 1:16 (joy and gladness — gil — "taken away"); Isa 16:10 (joy and gladness stripped from the fruitful field — gil). The structural opposite is expressed through the negation of the same vocabulary rather than a distinct antonym term.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Yes, by negation and by antonym: (1) **By negation** — "the Lord does not rejoice" (Isa 9:17 — sa.mach negated); "rejoice not" (Hos 9:1 — sa.mach prohibited); "let not your heart be glad" (Pro 24:17); (2) **By antonym** — mourning (Psa 30:11 — sackcloth removed; dancing given); sorrow (Joh 16:20 — sorrow → Joy); sighing (Isa 35:10 — sighing flees at Joy's arrival); grief (1Pe 1:6 — grief alongside Joy); darkness (Isa 24:11 — "all joy has grown dark"). The vocabulary does not have a single dedicated antonym term for Joy but uses the cluster of mourning/sorrow/sighing as its structural opposite across the corpus.

**[CHAR-7]** E — Yes: **mav.li.git** (H4010 — Jer 8:18: "my joy is gone; grief is upon me; my heart is sick within me") — the comfort/joy that is gone when Suffering-Joy's fragile form is entirely overwhelmed. Additionally: the world's rejoicing over the prophets' deaths (Rev 11:10 — chairo in the evil sense) is the structural-opposite of Suffering-Joy — the world's gladness at the silencing of truth.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Yes: **lo-tov** (negated tov — "not good") appears 15+ times in M04-L-VCG-02 and M04-O contexts (Exo 18:17; 1Sa 2:24; 2Sa 17:7; Neh 5:9; Pro 17:26; 18:5; 20:23; 24:23; 28:21; Eze 18:18; 20:25; 36:31; Isa 65:2) — the structural opposite is built into the primary term's own negation. This is analytically distinctive: unlike Joy (whose opposites are separate terms: mourning, sorrow), Gladness's structural opposite is simply the negation of its own primary term. This confirms that Gladness is constitutively an evaluative characteristic — its presence and absence are measured by the same standard.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Yes: (1) **lo-cha.phets** — "does not delight / takes no pleasure" (negated cha.phets): Psa 5:4; 40:6; 51:16; Isa 1:11; Jer 6:10; Heb 10:6, 8 — the structural opposite built into the primary verbal form's negation; (2) **mav.li.git** (H4010 — Jer 8:18) — also appearing in M04-F (Suffering-Joy); the comfort/joy that is entirely gone; (3) **Moab as a vessel for which no one cares** — Jer 48:38 (lo-che.phets) — the total absence of desire/care as social-relational rejection. The negated forms of both the verbal (cha.phets) and nominal (che.phets) registers provide structural-opposite vocabulary.

**[CHAR-5]** E — (1) **lo-ni.cho.ach** (negated ni.cho.ach) — Lev 26:31 ("I will not smell your pleasing aromas") — the structural opposite in the worship-Pleasure register: God's non-smelling = non-reception = absent worship-Pleasure; (2) **lo-a.las** (negated a.las) — Job 20:18 ("he will get no enjoyment") — the structural opposite of sensory Pleasure; (3) **Harshness** — implicitly the opposite of na.im/na.em's gentleness, though not a single dedicated opposite term.

**[CHAR-6]** E — Not a dedicated antonym, but: (1) **Forgetting as the structural opposite** — consistently named (Neh 9:17 — "not mindful"; Psa 78:11 — "forgot his works") rather than through a dedicated opposite-term; (2) **lo-pa.la** (negated) — Deu 30:11 ("this commandment is not too hard/wonderful for you") — the negation of pa.la indicating that something is not in the Wonder-category, accessible rather than exceeding; (3) **"No wonder"** — 2Cor 11:14 (thauma negated — "and no wonder") — the dismissal of Wonder by removing its unexpectedness.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The structural-opposite vocabulary across the cluster reveals a consistent pattern: most characteristics express their structural opposite through negation of their primary term (lo-tov for Gladness; lo-cha.phets for Delight; lo-ni.cho.ach for Pleasure) rather than through dedicated antonym terms. The exception is **Joy (Char 2)** — which has a rich cluster of opposite-terms (mourning, sorrow, sighing, grief, inner darkness) that are not simple negations but are named by distinct vocabulary. This confirms Joy as the characteristic whose opposite has the most developed vocabulary — mourning/grief as an inner-being domain with its own extensive terminology comparable to Joy's own. The cluster-wide pattern: the structural opposites are named (primarily through negation or adjacent grief-vocabulary) for all seven, confirming that the cluster is not merely positive-inner-being description but includes within its evidence base the diagnostic of inner-being dysfunction.

**[CHAR-1]** E — Yes. The structural opposite of shame is named through honour-vocabulary: *kabod* (glory/honour), *timē* (honour), *doxa* (glory) — these are not in the CHAR-1 corpus itself but appear in the contrast structures ("instead of your shame there shall be a double portion," Isa 61:7; "enemies clothed with shame but his crown shines," Psa 132:18). The term for the absence of shame is evidenced in the negative constructions: "you will not be ashamed" (future promise), "were not ashamed" (Gen 2:25), "will not be put to shame" (Psa 22:5 et al.) — the negated verb serves as the structural opposite vocabulary.

**[CHAR-2]** E — Rum (exalt, lift up) and nasa (lift) are the structural opposites named in the evidence: "he brings low and he exalts" (1Sa 2:7); "putting down one and lifting up another" (Psa 75:7). Kabod (glory, honor) is the state CHAR-2 replaces (Hos 4:7 — "change their glory into shame"; Hab 2:16 — "shame instead of glory").

**[CHAR-3]** E — Primary terms: Atimazō (G0818): to dishonour, treat as without honour — active verb, the dishonoring act. Atimia (G0819): dishonour as a state — the condition of assigned or received diminished worth. Entrepō (G1788) in its absence register: the failure of the regard-faculty. Paradeigmatizō (G3856): to expose publicly, hold up to contempt. Roots: a-timē — without honour, without worth — the alpha-privative of honour. Structural opposite: timaō (to honour, to assign worth) and timē (honour as assigned worth-recognition). The evidence pairs these explicitly in Joh 8:49. The CHAR-3 corpus is entirely NT — the OT vocabulary for relational worth-denial (qa.lah, H7034; entrepō in its absence register) is thinner. The NT's christological context gives CHAR-3 its sharpest definition: dishonour as what is directed at Jesus personally and at God through human hypocrisy. Person-type: the "unjust judge" (Luk 18:2) is the closest person-type but is not a technical term. Supplication: the widow's persistent coming to the judge (Luk 18:3) is a supplication for the reversal of CHAR-3 — the only supplication-context in the corpus.

**[CHAR-4]** E — Kalos (good, beautiful, proper) and euschēmosunē (decency, propriety, proper form — the opposite of aschēmosunē) are the structural opposites. The evidence implies these opposites: "by the open statement of the truth" (2Cor 4:2) vs. "shameful, underhanded ways"; "keeping his garments on" (Rev 16:15) vs. "going about naked and exposed."

**[CHAR-5]** E — The structural opposite of exoutheneō (treating as nothing) is acceptance — receiving the person as of genuine worth (Gal 4:14 — "received me as an angel of God"). The structural opposite of atimazō is timaō (to honour). The structural opposite of loidoria is eulogia (blessing — 1Pe 3:9: "do not repay reviling for reviling, but on the contrary bless").

**[CHAR-6]** E — The structural opposite of niq.qa.von (innocence/cleanness) is guilt or defilement — the inner moral condition that produces guilt-shame. The evidence names this opposite indirectly through Hos 8:5's "incapacity for innocence" — the state of having no access to the inner cleanness that innocence names.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's structural opposite vocabulary converges on honour and glory: timē (honour, G5092), kabod (glory, H3519), doxa (glory, G1391), and rum/nasa (exalt/lift — the Hebrew opposites of sha.phel). These appear consistently in the structural-opposite positions across all six characteristics. The honour-glory vocabulary is the unified counterpart to the shame-field: it is what shame displaces (Char 1 — "instead of your shame there shall be a double portion," Isa 61:7), what abasement reverses (Char 2 — "he brings low and he exalts," 1Sa 2:7), what dishonour withdraws (Char 3 — "I honor my Father, and you dishonor me," Joh 8:49), and what innocence enables approach toward (Char 6 — going around the altar, Psa 26:6).
