findings.finding_value: The full vocabulary arc of M01 — from ya.re / yir.ah / pa.chad (Hebrew) through fobeō / fobos / deilia / ekthambeo (Greek) — reveals that fear as described in Scripture spans a complete semantic range from: (1) the reverential inner disposition of the God-fearer (M01-A) — the highest, most ordered form; (2) the acute alarm of the person before overwhelming threat or divine encounter (M01-B) — situational, involuntary, episodic; (3) the overwhelming force of terror deployed against enemies (M01-C) — terror as a weapon with agency; (4) the shattering inner collapse of dismay (M01-D) — the person undone; (5) the body's involuntary trembling in registering fear or reverence (M01-E) — the somatic pole of the characteristic; (6) the chronic burden of anticipatory dread (M01-F) — fear extended forward in time; through to (7) the evaluatively condemned cowardly shrinking under pressure (M01-G) — the moral-failure pole. The arc reveals that fear in Scripture is the most comprehensive inner-being characteristic in the programme's cluster structure: it spans orientation, event, force, collapse, soma, duration, and moral evaluation — seven constitutive dimensions of a single unified characteristic. No other single programme cluster is anticipated to be as structurally comprehensive.

The full vocabulary arc reveals a characteristic that spans: (1) the most internal (spirit-level felt heat: Eze 3:14; Act 17:16); (2) through the intermediate (the anger-in-action: Exo 32:19; Neh 5:6); (3) to the structural (wrath as judicial verdict: Heb 3:11; Rom 1:18); (4) to the eschatological (the winepress of final judgment: Rev 19:15); (5) to the dispositional (the person-type: orgilos); (6) to the constitutive (divine jealousy as God's name: Exo 34:14). The arc runs from the deepest felt interior through every level of outward expression to the constitutional ground of the divine identity. This is one of the widest semantic arcs in the programme — the characteristic operates from the most interior to the most cosmic without losing its essential nature.

The full vocabulary arc of M03 (78 terms, 50 STAYS + 28 BOUNDARY) reveals that grief, sorrow, and mourning constitute one of the most semantically rich domains in the programme. The characteristic's complete range extends from: the immediate somatic expression (ba.khah, dim.ah, a.nach — the act of weeping/sighing/groaning) through the inner condition (ya.gon, tu.gah, perilupos — sorrow as settled inner state) through the acute overwhelming anguish (tsar, tsa.rah, sunochē — pressed/constricted) through the structured social form (sa.phad, mis.ped, e.vel — mourning as communal act) through the somatic-pain register (makh.ov, ke.ev, che.vel-B — pain as grief's phenomenological quality) through the qualitative texture (ma.ror, mam.ror — bitterness as grief's sharpest tone) to the purposive and generative registers (groaning toward redemption, godly grief toward repentance). The range is comprehensive across the full human experience of loss.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The full OT vocabulary arc reveals exultation as a comprehensive inner-being capacity with kinetic (gil — movement), affective-volitional (su.s — directed delight), and expressive (re.na.nah — triumphing cry) components that operate across all registers of the inner being's life: the person's spontaneous response to divine acts, the cultivated habit of Godward orientation, the volitional choice in adversity, the cosmic-scale participation of all creation, and God's own inner exultation over his people. The vocabulary arc is entirely OT-Hebrew in this sub-group, with NT continuity requiring cross-characteristic synthesis.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The full vocabulary arc across sa.mach/sim.chah (OT primary), sa.s.von (OT restoration), ma.s.vo.s (OT festive-communal), agalliao/agalliasis (eschatological-intense), chairo/chara (NT primary), sunchairo (NT co-joy), eucharistia (NT thanksgiving within Joy), and euthumeō (NT cheerfulness) reveals Joy as a characteristic with: (a) a stable core (active inner rejoicing in response to divine reality — carried by sa.mach/chairo across both testaments); (b) a festive-communal register (ma.s.vo.s; sunchairo — the social form of Joy); (c) an eschatological-restoration register (sa.s.von; agalliao — Joy oriented toward the not-yet); (d) a Spirit-mediated register (NT additions: the Spirit as Joy-agent); (e) an adjacent thanksgiving register (eucharistia — the Godward-gratitude face of Joy). The arc shows Joy as semantically rich, multi-registered, and consistently oriented across all registers toward genuine participation in what is celebratable before God.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The arc from ba.lag (OT fragile brightness) through mav.li.git (comfort-gone) to agalliao/agalliasis (NT Spirit-enabled intense exultation) reveals Suffering-Joy as a characteristic that exists in the OT in fragile, barely-attainable form and reaches its full expression in the NT through: (a) the Spirit's enabling; (b) the resurrection's eschatological grounding; (c) the Christ-pattern of suffering-to-glory as the normative trajectory. The characteristic is not an NT invention but the OT's barely-attempted cheerfulness brought to full, paradox-sustaining expression through the gospel.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The vocabulary arc of tov (OT primary, spanning divine character, moral appraisal, circumstantial benefit, and wellbeing) combined with makarismos (NT blessedness) and the adjacent sa.s.von (restoration-gladness) reveals Gladness as: (a) the most ontologically-grounded of M04's characteristics — tov's root in the concept of genuine goodness as objective quality makes Gladness the characteristic most directly connected to reality's moral structure; (b) the most cognitively-constituted — tov's evaluative-predicative grammar makes Gladness an assertion about what is genuinely the case, not merely a subjective feeling; (c) an OT-dominated characteristic — the near-absence of NT primary terms shows that the NT concentrated its positive inner-being development in Joy (chairo/chara) and Suffering-Joy (agalliao) rather than in the evaluative-gladness register.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The full vocabulary arc from sha.a.shu.im/sha.a/a.nog (affective-resting) through cha.phets/che.phets (volitional-sovereign) through arestos/ni.cho.ach (obedience-pleasing) through ta.a.nug (parental tenderness) through che.med/a.li.tsut (corrupt desire) reveals Delight as the most semantically complex and structurally comprehensive characteristic in M04. The arc spans from the most divinely transcendent (God's sovereign cha.phets declaring purpose — Isa 46:10) through the most intimately relational (Jer 31:20's sha.a.shu.im as God's cherishing of Ephraim-as-darling-child) through the most embodied (a.nog's luxuriating satisfaction) to the most corrupt (a.li.tsut's predatory elation). No other M04 characteristic spans this range.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The vocabulary arc reveals Pleasure as spanning the widest constitutional range in M04 (body to soul to God's inner being) through a diverse vocabulary: from the gentlest relational agreeableness (na.im — brotherly unity's pleasantness) through the worship-soothing mechanism (ni.cho.ach — the most technically specific worship-vocabulary in M04) through the bodily luxury-ease (a.nog — the most physically textured) through the wisdom-calibrated better-than (tov). The arc also reveals Pleasure as the characteristic with the largest worship-related technical vocabulary (the ni.cho.ach corpus of 38 verses), making it uniquely the characteristic most embedded in Israel's formal worship practice.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The pa.la/pe.le → thambeō/thaumazō arc reveals Wonder as a characteristic whose lexical identity is remarkably stable across the Testaments: the semantic content (inner seizure before what is categorically extraordinary) is preserved across the Hebrew and Greek vocabularies. What changes is the primary object: the OT's dominant wonder-object is God's acts in Exodus and creation history; the NT's dominant wonder-object is Jesus himself — his teaching, authority, and advance. The arc reveals Wonder as moving from acts (OT) to person (NT): in the NT, encountering Jesus produces Wonder more directly than encountering his acts, pointing toward the revelation of the Wonderful Counselor as the fullness of all divine wonder.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The full vocabulary arc across all seven characteristics reveals three master-movements: (1) **From acts to Person** — the cluster's OT vocabulary primarily names God's extraordinary acts as the objects of Wonder, Joy, Exultation, and Gladness; the NT shifts toward Jesus himself as the primary object; the Wonderful Counselor (Isa 9:6 — pe.le applied to a person rather than acts) bridges this transition; (2) **From fragile to Spirit-enabled** — the OT's ba.lag (fragile brightness) becomes the NT's agalliao (Spirit-enabled intense exultation); the OT's barely-attained comfort under suffering is replaced by the NT's paradox-sustaining rejoicing through the Spirit; (3) **From individual to community** — the NT's sunchairo (co-rejoicing), the NT's focus on the gathered community's Suffering-Joy (Act 5:41; 16:34), and the NT's expansion of Joy's relational scope all show the cluster's communal dimension deepened and institutionalised in the NT period. The three master-movements together confirm the cluster as covenantal-historical in its development: its vocabulary, object, and scope all expand and deepen from OT through NT.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The full vocabulary arc reveals CHAR-1 as a characteristic deeply embedded in both Testaments' inner-being vocabulary, primarily through the *bosh* family in Hebrew and the *aischun-* family in Greek. The arc shows the characteristic's stability across testamental contexts: shame is shame — the inner collapse of dignity before exposure, failure, or moral inadequacy — in both Testaments, and the vocabulary confirms this without significant discontinuity. The NT's christological focus (Heb 12:2; 2Cor 10:8; Phili 1:20) represents the most significant development: shame is now specifically engaged with the believer's relation to Christ and his cross.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The vocabulary arc runs from the OT's concrete social-bodily humiliation (ka.lam — shaved beards, covered heads) through wisdom tradition's moral-consequence pairing (pride -> qa.lon) through prophetic Day-of-the-Lord cosmic bringing-low (sha.phel in the Isa 2 series) to the NT's eschatological frame (atimia of mortal existence -> resurrection glory). The arc reveals CHAR-2 as operating at every level of human existence — bodily, social, national, cosmic — with its final resolution eschatological.

**[CHAR-3]** E — Primary terms: Atimazō (G0818): to dishonour, treat as without honour — active verb, the dishonoring act. Atimia (G0819): dishonour as a state — the condition of assigned or received diminished worth. Entrepō (G1788) in its absence register: the failure of the regard-faculty. Paradeigmatizō (G3856): to expose publicly, hold up to contempt. Roots: a-timē — without honour, without worth — the alpha-privative of honour. Structural opposite: timaō (to honour, to assign worth) and timē (honour as assigned worth-recognition). The evidence pairs these explicitly in Joh 8:49. The CHAR-3 corpus is entirely NT — the OT vocabulary for relational worth-denial (qa.lah, H7034; entrepō in its absence register) is thinner. The NT's christological context gives CHAR-3 its sharpest definition: dishonour as what is directed at Jesus personally and at God through human hypocrisy. Person-type: the "unjust judge" (Luk 18:2) is the closest person-type but is not a technical term. Supplication: the widow's persistent coming to the judge (Luk 18:3) is a supplication for the reversal of CHAR-3 — the only supplication-context in the corpus.

---

**[CHAR-4]** E — The vocabulary arc runs from the OT's shameful-object/idolatry register (bo.shet naming the idol as "the shameful thing" in Jer 3:24; 11:13) through the NT's conscience-evaluative register (aischros, aschēmosunē in 1Cor, Eph, Tit) to the inverted-conscience register (aischunē as gloried-in shame in Phili 3:19). The arc reveals CHAR-4 as operating across both Testaments in morally consistent terms: the evaluative standard remains God's holiness throughout; the corruption of the evaluative faculty takes different forms but is consistently identified as dangerous to the person's eschatological standing.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The vocabulary arc moves from the OT's ka.lam in its protection-from-reproach register (Rut 2:15; 1Sa 25:7/15) through the NT's exoutheneō-dominated contempt-vocabulary (VCG-01) to the christological-reversal language (Act 4:11; 1Cor 1:28). The arc reveals CHAR-5 as a characteristic whose OT evidence is primarily protective (shielding from contempt) and whose NT evidence is primarily christological (Jesus receiving contempt, Jesus reversing contempt-verdicts). The trajectory is from protection toward transformation.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The vocabulary arc for CHAR-6 is compact and exclusively OT: four verse-records, two terms (niq.qa.von and qe.ha.von), appearing in narrative (Gen 20:5), worship-psalm (Psa 26:6), lament-psalm (Psa 73:13), and prophecy (Hos 8:5). The arc reveals CHAR-6 as a characteristic defined by its OT cultic-covenant context: the inner moral innocence that enables approach to God in the worship context. The arc's movement from the functioning-innocence-enabling-approach (Gen 20:5; Psa 26:6) through the questioned-innocence-under-suffering (Psa 73:13) to the incapacity-for-innocence (Hos 8:5) reveals the full range of CHAR-6's operation: from its positive functioning through its testing to its loss.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's vocabulary arc moves through four phases. (1) OT foundational: bosh, bo.shet, ka.lam, ke.lim.mah, sha.phel establishing the experiential, social, and judicial shame registers. (2) OT prophetic promise: the shame-removal vocabulary (Isa 54:4; 61:7; Joe 2:26-27; Zep 3:19) establishing the eschatological orientation. (3) NT christological: exoutheneō, atimazō, and the passion vocabulary applying the shame-field to Christ's reception, rejection, and reversal. (4) NT community-ethics: the epistolary vocabulary (Cor, Rom, Pet, Tit) applying the shame-evaluative vocabulary to community formation, moral calibration, and inter-community worth-recognition. The arc reveals M07 as a cluster with deep OT roots that receives christological intensification in the NT and is applied to community formation through the epistolary literature.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The full vocabulary arc — spanning at least 20 distinct Hebrew and Greek terms in the 149-verse CHAR-1 corpus — reveals that arrogant self-elevation is one of the most lexically rich characteristics in the programme's evidence base. The semantic range covers: (a) Spatial-metaphorical (height/elevation): rum (H7311A/H7312), ga.vah (H1361), ga.on (H1347), ga.vo.ah (H1364), ma.rom (H4791), qo.mah (H6967), hupsēlos (G5308) — the core upward-movement metaphor; (b) Dispositional quality: ga.a.vah (H1346), ge.vah (H1466), ge.ah (H1344), ga.on (H1347), huperēfania (G5243) — the settled inner posture; (c) Person-type: ge.eh (H1343), ga.vo.ah (H1364), huperēfanos (G5244), sha.chats (H7830 — fierce self-asserting creatures) — the one who characteristically bears CHAR-1; (d) Volitional-act: rum (verb active), ga.ah (H1342 — to rise), ga.vah (verb) — the act of self-elevation; (e) Root-motivation: filautos (G5367) — the generative self-love orientation; (f) Social-appearance: huperēfanos (G5244) — the one who presents above others. The arc from Hebrew spatial metaphor to Greek social-comparative to NT motivational root reveals a progressive analytical refinement across the Testaments, with the Hebrew establishing the spatial metaphor and the NT developing the social and motivational precision.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The full vocabulary arc across zid, za.don, zed (OT) and authadēs, tolmētēs, archō (NT) reveals CHAR-2 as a characteristic with a narrower but more precisely targeted semantic range than CHAR-1. The range covers: (a) act register: zid (the boiling-over act), archō (the initiation of the presumptuous action); (b) dispositional quality: za.don (the insolent inner quality), authadēs (the self-willed orientation); (c) person-type: zed (the insolent person), tolmētēs (the recklessly bold person); (d) prayer-resistance term: Psa 19:13 (presumptuous sins as object of resistant prayer). The vocabulary arc is consistent: all terms name the self-authorising will's transgression of an established authority, from different angles (act, quality, type, motivational root). The NT adds motivational precision (authadēs) and extends the scope to spiritual beings (tolmētēs).

**[CHAR-3]** E — The full vocabulary arc — ha.lal, ro.hav (OT) and kauchaomai/kauchēma/kauchēsis, alazoneia/alazōn (NT) — reveals CHAR-3 as the M08 characteristic with the broadest positive valence within its vocabulary: the kauchaomai family spans condemnation (VCG-01), examination (VCG-02), and commendation (VCG-03). This is unique in M08: no other characteristic's primary vocabulary spans all three moral evaluations with the same terms. The arc reveals that the glorying/boasting capacity is not inherently evil but direction-dependent — making CHAR-3 the M08 characteristic closest to the M22 praise-register at the vocabulary level.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The full vocabulary arc (fusioō, tufoō, fusiōsis, huperfroneō) reveals CHAR-4 as the most lexically focused of the M08 characteristics: four terms, all from the same cognitive-inflation semantic domain, with no cross-register spanning (unlike CHAR-1's rum/ga.on or CHAR-3's kauchaomai). The arc consistently names: cognitive inflation without actual substance (fusioō), cognitive obscuration by self-generated smoke (tufoō), the measure-exceeding cognitive act (huperfroneō), and the communal disorder this produces (fusiōsis). The vocabulary arc is entirely NT and entirely Pauline (except 2Ti's tufoō), confirming CHAR-4 as a characteristic distinctively developed in the NT's engagement with community formation.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The full vocabulary arc — ga.on, ma.rom, ga.vah, shal.le.tet, a.din, qo.mah (OT) and hupsēlofroneō (NT) — reveals CHAR-5 as the most structurally diverse vocabulary set in M08: seven distinct terms spanning the collective (ga.on — national proud might), the spatial (ma.rom, qo.mah — height), the dispositional (ga.vah — heart-pride), the volitional (shal.le.tet — imperious self-will), the affective (a.din — voluptuous ease), and the cognitive-individual (hupsēlofroneō). This breadth reflects CHAR-5's multi-dimensional character: it operates through the widest range of structural media (military, geographic, economic, political, affective) of any M08 characteristic. The arc confirms CHAR-5 as M08's structural-power register — the characteristic that engages all the faculties (dispositional, volitional, cognitive, affective) through the specific medium of received structural goods.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's complete vocabulary arc across all five characteristics reveals three overarching patterns. First, spatial dominance: the core metaphorical system of M08 is spatial elevation — rum, ga.on, ga.vah, ga.a.vah, huperēfanos, hupsēlos, ma.rom, qo.mah all name upward movement beyond proper creaturely station. The cluster's vocabulary is constitutively spatial. Second, cross-register spanning: the g-'-h and r-w-m roots and kauchaomai/ha.lal all span M08 and M22 (divine majesty), confirming the etymological parasitism of pride on divine greatness vocabulary. Third, NT precision development: the NT consistently adds psychological and social precision to the OT's spatial and moral vocabulary — moving from "the high person" (OT) to "the self-pleasing person" (authadēs), "the inflated person" (fusioō), "the above-measure thinker" (huperfroneō), and "the wealth-haughty person" (hupsēlofroneō). The cluster-synthesis: M08's vocabulary arc is one of the programme's richest and most systematically structured — moving from Hebrew spatial root-families through Hellenistic social vocabulary to Pauline precision compounds.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The full vocabulary arc (yiq.qe.hah → hupakoē → hupakouō → hupotagē) reveals a characteristic that spans: *act* (obeying), *quality* (obedience as inner disposition), *condition* (being ordered under), *person-type* (obedient children). The semantic range covers eschatological (Gen49:10), wisdom-moral (Pro30:17), Christological (Heb5:8; Rom5:19), gospel-responsive (Rom1:5; Act6:7), household-formational (Eph6:1; 1Ti3:4), and soul-purifying (1Pe1:22) registers. The arc confirms the characteristic's central and wide-ranging role in the inner-being landscape — it is not a peripheral virtue but a structural one that appears wherever the person is in relation to legitimate authority, from the most immediate household to the cosmic-eschatological.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The vocabulary arc is confined to two appearances of dak.ka across two verses. The arc reveals: *person-type* (crushed in spirit, brokenhearted — Psa34:18; contrite and lowly spirit — Isa57:15); *spirit-level location* (both verses); *heart-level location* (Psa34:18 — brokenhearted). The arc is deliberately narrow — one term, two appearances — which confirms the characteristic's thin evidentiary base and the need for cross-canonical investigation to complete the vocabulary portrait. The absence of NT Greek evidence suggests the characteristic's fuller articulation may require tracking the Hebrew register across the full OT canon and its NT receptions in repentance and brokenness vocabulary.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The vocabulary arc (metriopatheō + okneō) reveals a characteristic constituted by two complementary terms: one naming the quality of engagement (measured-within-bounds compassion) and one naming the quality of will (non-hesitating readiness). The arc is narrow (two terms, two appearances) but the two terms together cover a distinctive inner-being profile: the person who engages gently with the erring and responds promptly without self-protective delay is comprehensively described by this pair. The absence of Hebrew OT terms in the corpus is the most significant evidence gap in the vocabulary arc — it limits the OT-NT comparison and suggests CHAR-4 may need expanded registry coverage to complete the vocabulary portrait.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The vocabulary arc is narrow (one term, three appearances) but analytically significant: semnotēs across three contexts (civic, household, pedagogical) reveals a characteristic with comprehensive social-ordering reach. The arc confirms: the characteristic is a *noun-of-quality* (stable inner character property); it operates across the full range of the believer's social existence ("in every way" — 1Ti2:2); it has no internal vocabulary differentiation (single term for all aspects). The absence of Hebrew OT vocabulary is the most significant gap — the characteristic's OT antecedents (if any) are not registered in M09 and would require expanded registry work.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The vocabulary arc (five appearances of na.div across three OT books — Exodus, Chronicles, Psalms) reveals a characteristic with consistent meaning across historical, narrative, and lyrical contexts: (a) *person-type* (1Ch28:21 — every willing man); (b) *quality of constitutional location* (Exo35:5/22; 2Ch29:31 — willing heart; Psa51:12 — willing spirit); (c) *supplication* (Psa51:12 — seeking the willing spirit from God). The arc spans tabernacle-construction (Exo35), temple-service preparation (1Ch28:21), temple-restoration worship (2Ch29:31), and personal penitential prayer (Psa51:12). The OT-only evidence base is the most significant limitation of the arc — the NT development of this register is not represented in the programme's na.div corpus.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The full vocabulary arc (ka.na → tsa.na/tsa.nu.a → tapeinos → tapeinofrosunē → tapeinoō → tapeinōsis) reveals a characteristic that spans: *act* (ka.na verbal, tapeinoō), *disposition* (tapeinofrosunē, tsa.nu.a as adjective), *condition* (tapeinōsis, tsa.na as state), *person-quality* (tapeinos as adjective). The semantic range covers *voluntary and imposed*, *inner-act and outer-condition*, *OT-covenantal and NT-Christological*, *wisdom-epistemic and community-relational*, and *present-dispositional and eschatological-anticipatory* registers. The arc is comprehensive — the characteristic operates across every register of the inner being's posture before God and others, which confirms its foundational role in the inner-being landscape (T6.1.2 — humility as meta-characteristic enabling the operation of multiple other characteristics).

**[CLUSTER]** E — The full vocabulary arc spans four OT Hebrew term-families (ka.na, dak.ka, na.div, yiq.qe.hah) and five NT Greek term-families (tapein-, hupakoē/hupakouō/hupotagē, metriopatheō, okneō, semnotēs). The arc reveals three structural findings. (a) OT-to-NT developmental direction: OT vocabulary is more event-oriented and crisis-oriented (ka.na — act of humbling; dak.ka — crushed state; na.div — freely-springing inner movement); NT vocabulary is more disposition-oriented and social-ordering (tapeinofrosunē — stable character disposition; semnotēs — social-ordering gravity; metriopatheō — calibrated engagement quality). (b) Testamental distribution by characteristic type: the most acute/crisis characteristics (CHAR-3 — dak.ka) and most spontaneous (CHAR-6 — na.div) are OT-only; the most social-ordering (CHAR-4, CHAR-5) are NT-only; the most foundational (CHAR-1, CHAR-2) span both testaments and show NT coinage development (tapeinofrosunē; hupotagē as NT-period valorisations). (c) NT coinage significance: tapeinofrosunē (CHAR-1) and hupotagē (CHAR-2) are NT-period developments that valorise as virtues what Greco-Roman culture treated as deficiencies — the NT community needed new vocabulary to name M09's characteristics as positive because their cultural environment did not. This is M09's most significant lexical contribution to the NT vocabulary.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The full vocabulary arc — from cha.ta's physical "missing" (Judg 20:16) through its covenantal "sinning against God" (Eze 14:13), through the LXX hamartanō bridge, into the NT's "sin against your brother" (Mat 18:15) and "sin against your own body" (1Cor 6:18), to the paraptōma "entanglement" (Gal 6:1) — reveals that wilful sinning covers the entire relational map of the human person (God, others, self) across its full directional range (deliberate, entangled, sustained). The semantic arc also reveals that sinning is consistently treated as an *act with consequences* at every point — the vocabulary never becomes purely abstract or dispositional.

**[CHAR-10]** E — The vocabulary arc — three distinct Greek terms (deleazō/bait-lure, sunupokrinomai/collective-acting, apostasia/standing-away-from) covering desire-exploitation (Jam 1:14; 2Pe 2:14/18), collective identity-performance (Gal 2:13), and covenantal-departure (Act 21:21) — reveals a characteristic whose vocabulary is diverse but united by a common analytical insight: these are the *specific inner mechanisms* through which sin operates. Each term names a precise mechanism rather than a general category of sinning. The arc reveals: the NT period was conceptually attentive to the *how* of sin — the specific pathways, processes, and mechanisms — in a way that produced dedicated vocabulary for three distinct sinning mechanisms.

**[CHAR-11]** E — The vocabulary arc — from chat.tat's crouching predator (Gen 4:7 — OT origin-point) through rish.ah's settled wickedness-identity (Isa 9:18; Mal 1:4/3:15/4:1) through hamartia's redemption register (VCG-02 — forgiveness declared) through hamartia's cosmic-power register (VCG-03 — enslaving power, indwelling force, governing law) — reveals the characteristic's complete semantic field: the universal condition as (1) a predatory entity desiring dominion, (2) a settled inner wickedness-character, (3) a debt requiring divine forgiveness, and (4) a cosmic enslaving power requiring the death and resurrection of Christ to defeat. The arc is the most comprehensive in M10: it spans the full range of how the condition is conceptualised from Genesis through Paul's systematic development in Romans.

**[CHAR-12]** E — The vocabulary arc — from hamartia-as-owner (Joh 8:34 — *doulos tēs hamartias*) through hamartia-as-imprisoner (Gal 3:22 — *hypo hamartian*) through hamartanō-as-practice (1Jo 3:8/9 — present participial forms) through the liberation-vocabulary (born of God — 1Jo 3:9; 5:18) — reveals a characteristic whose vocabulary maps the *full governance-cycle of sin's enslaving power*: sin owns (Joh 8:34), sin confines (Gal 3:22), sin is practised in continuous present (1Jo 3:8), and liberation comes through divine birth that constitutionally prevents the continuous sinning (1Jo 3:9). The arc is a complete theological grammar of enslavement and liberation.

**[CHAR-13]** E — The vocabulary arc — from chat.tat's individual act-as-fact (Lev 4:23 — "the sin which he has committed") through chet's personal-bearing (Num 9:13 — "bear his sin") through cha.ta.ah's heart-inscription (Jer 17:1 — "engraved on the tablet of their heart") through the storage/book metaphors (Hos 13:12 — "kept in store"; Exo 32:32 — "your book") through the erasure vocabulary (Isa 43:25 — blotted out; Mic 7:19 — cast into the sea) to Joh 1:29's totalization ("the sin of the world" lifted by the Lamb) — reveals a characteristic whose vocabulary maps the complete divine-record lifecycle: creation of the entry, personal bearing, internal inscription, divine storage, escalating consequences, and finally eschatological erasure.

**[CHAR-14]** E — The vocabulary arc — from kāpar's covering-mechanism (OT — the sin covered by sacrifice) through chat.tat's sin-offering institution (OT — the animal bearing the sin) through aphesis's divine release-declaration (NT — God releasing the debt) through hamartia's forgiveness-scope (NT — the sin of the world whose Lamb takes it away — Joh 1:29) through paraptōma's not-counted-trespass (NT — 2Cor 5:19) — reveals a characteristic whose vocabulary moves from institutional-mechanism (how atonement is performed) to declarative-event (the moment of divine release). The arc is: ritual institution → sacrificial mechanism → priestly covering → divine declaration of release → permanent redemption-identity.

**[CHAR-15]** E — The vocabulary arc — exclusively cha.ta (H2398) deployed across founding-ancestral (Isa 43:27 — "your first father sinned"), escalating-continuation (Psa 78:17 — "sinned still more"), persistent-unbelief (Psa 78:32 — "still sinned despite wonders"), prolonged-duration (Isa 64:5 — "a long time in our sins"), corporate-doom-cause (Jer 8:14 — "because we have sinned"), divine-rescue (Eze 37:23 — "backslidings in which they have sinned"), and eschatological-curse (Isa 65:20 — the sinner cursed) — reveals a characteristic whose entire vocabulary range is the temporal and contextual depth of the universal sinning verb. The arc covers the complete generational sequence: origin → escalation → prolonged condition → doom → confession → divine rescue → eschatological resolution, all through a single verb applied across the generational time-span.

**[CHAR-16]** E — The vocabulary arc — from chat.ta's intensive-agent characterisation of extreme sinners (OT — Gen 13:13; Sodom; Amalekites) through hamartōlos's social-stigma category (NT synoptic — tax collectors and sinners at table) through the self-aware sinner's plea (Luk 5:8; Luk 18:13) through the federal constitution of all as sinners (Rom 5:19 — "made sinners") through the foremost-sinner paradigm (1Ti 1:15) — reveals a characteristic whose vocabulary charts the complete moral-identity spectrum: from extreme habitual type (chat.ta — OT) to socially recognised category (hamartōlos — synoptic) to constituted universal standing (hamartōlos — Pauline) to self-aware individual identity (hamartōlos — Luk 5:8; 18:13). The arc covers every mode through which the sinner-identity can be held.

**[CHAR-17]** E — The vocabulary arc — from a.sham's guilt-recognition verb (Lev 5:5 — the conscience-engagement moment) through ash.mah's accumulated guilt-condition (Ezr 9:6 — mounting to the heavens) through a.von H5771H's transferable guilt-burden (Exo 28:38 — Aaron bearing Israel's guilt on his forehead) through a.von H5771I's punitive-consequence dimension (Gen 4:13 — punishment greater than Cain can bear; Eze 4:4/5/6 — prophet bearing Israel's punishment) through pu.qah's conscience-stagger (1Sa 25:31 — pangs of conscience) through ash.mah's indelibility (Jer 2:22 — stain before God despite soap) to Isa 6:7's removal (guilt taken away) — reveals a characteristic whose vocabulary covers the complete guilt-arc from its conscience-recognition origin through its accumulation and weight through its transference and punishment-bearing to its indelible divine-visibility and finally its removal by divine act.

**[CHAR-18]** E — The vocabulary arc — a single term (a.von H5771G) across 162 verses from Gen 15:16 (Amorites' iniquity not yet complete — measurability) through Exo 20:5 (generational transmission) through Lev 16:21/22 (priestly scapegoat ritual — transference) through Psa 38:4 (overwhelming weight) through Isa 53:5/6/11 (servant bearing the iniquity of all — typological climax) through Jer 31:34 (new covenant forgiveness — eschatological resolution) through Zec 3:9 (iniquity of the land removed in a single day) to Mal 2:6 (faithful priest turning many from iniquity) — reveals the full moral-crime arc of accumulated iniquity in OT theology: from its measurable accumulation (Gen 15:16) through its overwhelming weight (Psa 38:4) to its vicarious bearing by the servant (Isa 53) to its new covenant dissolution (Jer 31:34). The single-term consistency across the full arc confirms CHAR-18 as the OT's primary vocabulary for the objective moral-crime accumulation that culminates in the servant's bearing.

**[CHAR-19]** E — The full vocabulary arc — from pe.sha's relational rebellion (Gen 31:36 — interpersonal; Isa 1:2 — "they have rebelled against me") through sa.rah's inner defiance (Isa 1:5 — "whole head sick and whole heart faint" from continued revolt) through the Amos threshold-counting (Amos 1:3 — "three and four") through Isa 53:5/8's servant pierced for transgressions through Dan 9:24's appointed finish through parabasis's law-violation precision (Rom 4:15) through paraptōma's Adam-paradigm (Rom 5:15/16/17/18/20) — reveals the complete arc of deliberate boundary-crossing from its first instance (Adam's trespass) through its OT relational-rebellion register through its eschatological appointed finish (Dan 9:24) through its NT legal precision to its resolution through the servant's bearing.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The vocabulary arc — cha.ta + bishgagah (inadvertent sinning), shegagah (error), a.von (iniquity borne, Lev 5:1), chat.ta.ah (sin offering, Lev 9:15), cha.ta Piel (to purify, VCG-02) — reveals that CHAR-2's semantic range covers the full sweep from the inadvertent act through the resulting moral condition to the institutional remedy and its application to sacred spaces. The arc is *act → condition → remedy → restoration*, each stage named by distinct vocabulary. The full arc also reveals the characteristic's confinement to the OT Hebrew context: the *bishgagah* qualifier and the Levitical remedial vocabulary are OT-specific, and the NT's absence from this corpus confirms that the characteristic is most precisely defined and evidenced within the Hebrew covenantal system.

**[CHAR-20]** E — The vocabulary arc — from Exo 21:8 (ma.al — breaking faith with a designated woman) through Lev 5:15/6:2 (ma.al — cultic breach of faith against holy things and God) through Num 5:12/27 (ma.al/ba.gad — marital faithlessness ordeal) through Jos 7:1/22:16-31 (ma.al — covenant-breach of the ban; Achan-to-Israel) through Chronicles' sustained ma.al-history (1Ch 9:1/10:13; 2Ch 12:2/26:16/28:19/22/29:6/30:7/36:14) through Ezra's communal confession (ma.al — Ezr 9:2/4/10:2/6/10) through the Psalms/Proverbs ba.gad-portrait of the traitor (Psa 25:3/119:158; Pro 11:3/6/13:2/15) through Isaiah's constitutional-character treachery (Isa 21:2/24:16/33:1/48:8) through Jeremiah/Ezekiel's covenant-betrayal accusation (Jer 3:20/5:11; Eze 14:13/17:20/39:23) through Malachi's spirit-vigilance command (Mal 2:14/15/16) — reveals the complete OT covenantal-faithlessness arc from individual sacred-trespass through marital-covenant-breach through national covenant-betrayal to constitutional inner character.

**[CHAR-21]** E — The vocabulary arc — from sa.laph's judgment-subversion (Exo 23:8 — bribery overturning justice) through tah.pu.khah's speech-perversion (Pro 6:14 — perverted heart; Pro 8:13 — wisdom hating perverseness) through a.vah's personal moral-twisting (1Ki 8:47; Dan 9:5 — "acted perversely") through te.vel's created-order violation (Lev 18:23 — bestiality as perversion) through sur's degenerative vine-turning (Jer 2:21) through cha.val's destructive corruption (Neh 1:7; Isa 32:7) through ftheirō's progressive desire-corruption (Eph 4:22) through diaftheirō's comprehensive mind-depravity (1Ti 6:5) through fthora's cosmic bondage-to-corruption (Rom 8:21) to Rev 19:2's judgment of the cosmic corrupting agent — reveals M10's most terminologically diverse characteristic spanning all levels from individual judgment-perception through speech through personal moral-twisting through created-category-violation through cosmic decay to eschatological judgment.

**[CHAR-22]** E — The vocabulary arc — from a.vel's judicial prohibition (Lev 19:15 — "do no injustice in court") through av.lah's violent-oppression register (Psa 58:2 — "your hands deal out violence") through av.val's person-type naming (Job 27:7/29:17 — "the unrighteous") through adikos's NT person-type precision (1Cor 6:9 — "the unrighteous will not inherit"; 1Pe 3:18 — "the righteous for the unrighteous") through adikēma's legal-crime specificity (Act 18:14; Rev 18:5) — reveals the complete arc of injustice from its most concrete prohibitions (judicial, commercial) through its person-type constitution to its legal-theological precision and eschatological reckoning. The arc confirms CHAR-22 as M10's most institutionally specific characteristic and M26's direct antonym-partner.

**[CHAR-3]** E — The vocabulary arc — *chatati* (I have sinned: OT individual), *chatanu* (we have sinned: OT corporate), *yadat* (to know: cognitive ground of confession, 2Sa 19:20), the heart-struck idiom (2Sa 24:10: affective-conscience ground), *na* + *selach* (please + forgive: supplication following), *lo yizzaker* (not remembered: divine response, Eze 33:16), *hēmarton* (NT: I sinned, same semantic structure) — reveals that the confession vocabulary is not a dedicated lexical field but the sinning vocabulary deployed in the self-application mode. The arc covers: the cognitive-conscience base, the verbal act, the supplication that follows, and the divine response. Together they map the complete moral episode of which confession is the pivot: sin named (confessed) → mercy sought (plea) → record cancelled (forgiveness).

**[CHAR-4]** E — The vocabulary arc — from *lo chatati* (I have not sinned — Jer 2:35: active denial) through *hachotet* (the sinner — Ecc 8:12: person-type) through *hamartanō* continuous (1Cor 15:34: ongoing action in stupor) to *exestraptai* (warped — Tit 3:11: deposit consequence) — reveals that conscience suppression is expressed at every stage of the sinning vocabulary: denial of the act, constitution of the type, continuation of the pattern, and deformation of character. The full arc maps the characteristic's progression: the suppression begins as a denial or absence (act-level) and ends as a deformation (character-level). The vocabulary across both Testaments uses the same root domain but captures different phases of the same progressive deterioration.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The vocabulary arc — from *lo sur min* (OT negated departure: he did not depart from) through *davaq* (clung to) through *qasha/sarar* (stiffened neck/stubborn shoulder) through *hamartanōn* continuous (NT persisting in sin) through *hekousiōs hamartanontōn* (NT sinning deliberately) — reveals that refusal to repent is expressed at every stage of the characteristic's development: the passive non-departure (lo sur), the active attachment (davaq), the constitutional hardening (qasha/sarar), the ongoing action (hamartanōn continuous), and the deliberate volitional choice against known truth (hekousiōs). The full arc maps the characteristic from its mildest (passive non-departure) to its most severe (deliberate volitional sinning after knowing truth), with the vocabulary itself tracking the progressive intensification.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The vocabulary arc — from universal sinning (1Ki 8:46; Ecc 7:20 — "no one who does not sin") through person-type (hachotet — the sinner as constituted type — Ecc 7:26; 9:2/18; Pro 11:31/13:22) through iterative pattern (Exo 9:34 — "sinned yet again and hardened") through historical-generational persistence (Hos 10:9 — from Gibeah continued) through communal destruction (Ecc 9:18 — one sinner destroys much good) through NT continuous-state (1Jo 3:6 — "keeps on sinning / never seen or known him") — reveals a characteristic whose vocabulary tracks every stage of its development: universal susceptibility → individual person-type → iterative act → historical pattern → communal consequence → relational-epistemic verdict. The arc is the most comprehensive temporal sweep of any characteristic's vocabulary in the M10 corpus.

**[CHAR-7]** E — The vocabulary arc — Hiphil causative of cha.ta deployed across three mechanisms (authority: 1Ki 16:2; structural construction: Jer 32:35; teaching: Deu 20:18) through the full span of the Kings narrative from Jeroboam's initial transmission to Josiah's structural reversal (2Ki 23:15) — reveals a characteristic whose vocabulary is singular and precise: the Hiphil causative is CHAR-7's exclusive identifier. The arc covers: preventive naming (Exo 23:33; Deu 20:18), historical transmission (1Ki 14:16 through 2Ki 21:16), and structural reversal (2Ki 23:15). The vocabulary arc tracks the entire life of the Jeroboam pattern from prophetic warning through national consequence to physical dismantling — a ~300-year narrative horizon expressed through a single grammatical form.

**[CHAR-8]** E — The vocabulary arc — pa.sha exclusively, across all 9 verses, covering ongoing condition (1Ki 12:19), specific event (2Ki 1:1/3:5), military-politically significant occasion (2Ki 3:7), revolt-plus-independence-establishment (2Ki 8:20), and "to this day" permanent condition (2Ki 8:22; 2Ch 10:19; 2Ch 21:10) — reveals that CHAR-8 is the most vocabularily homogeneous characteristic in the M10 corpus. The exclusive use of a single root across 9 verses without any alternate vocabulary confirms that the characteristic is definitionally narrow: it is exactly what pa.sha names in its political register, nothing more and nothing less. The arc covers the full temporal range of the act: from specific event through ongoing condition to permanent fracture.

**[CHAR-9]** E — The vocabulary arc — from person-directed slander (VCG-01 — Eph 4:31/Col 3:8 — community context) through divine-authority usurpation (VCG-02 — Mat 12:31/Mar 2:7/Joh 10:33 — christological context) through constitutive anti-God defiance (VCG-03 — Rev 13:1/5/6/17:3 — eschatological context) — reveals that blasfēmia names a single unified semantic field: speech that harms by claiming, usurping, or defying what is not the speaker's to claim, usurp, or defy. The arc covers the full range from relational-interpersonal harm (slander) through theological-judicial claim (blasphemy) to cosmic-constitutive defiance (the beast). The unifying thread is harmful speech from inner corruption directed at relational targets (persons or God).

**[CHAR-1]** E — The full vocabulary arc (ra.sha person-type, re.sha abstract condition, mir.sha.at collective, rasha' verbal act, tsaddiq structural opposite, plus the ro.a adjective-of-badness) reveals that this characteristic's semantic range is comprehensive at the person-moral-identity level: it names the person, the person's inner condition, the collective of such persons, the act that expresses the condition, and the structural opposite that defines it by contrast. The arc is self-contained and fully developed within the Hebrew OT vocabulary — it does not require NT Greek supplementation to be analytically complete. The OT has built a complete moral-anthropological vocabulary for the wicked person as an inner-being type. The characteristic's semantic range is therefore as wide as the full RSH-root vocabulary suite plus the contextually associated terms (tsaddiq as opposite; iniquity terms as co-occurring conditions).

**[CHAR-2]** E — The full vocabulary arc (ponēros + kakia + adikia + ponēria + faulos) reveals a semantic range that spans: evil as a broad moral quality (ponēros — most comprehensive), evil as settled hostile inner residue (kakia — most constitutional), evil as structural wrongness (adikia — most relational to the moral order), evil as active malicious wickedness (ponēria — most volitionally aggressive), and evil as morally worthless deeds (faulos — most behavioural-evaluative). Together these five terms cover the full spectrum from constitutional condition to specific expression, from inner residue to outward act, from structural wrongness to active malice. The vocabulary arc is complete: it provides a lexical map of the constitutional inner evil at every level from its deepest structural reality (adikia) through its settled character (kakia) to its broadest qualitative expression (ponēros).

**[CHAR-3]** E — The full arc (to.e.vah + bdelugma + bdeluktos) reveals a semantic range spanning: (1) the divine-verdict category (to.e.vah as the standard term for what provokes divine revulsion); (2) the sensory-disgust quality of that revulsion (bdelugma — what stinks morally); (3) the person-type who embodies the abominable quality (bdeluktos); (4) the inner-character content that triggers the verdict (crooked heart, arrogant heart, lying lips, dishonest practice, perverted judgment, corrupt worship); (5) the relational consequence of the verdict (exclusion from divine intimacy, unacceptable worship, eschatological exclusion). The vocabulary arc is complete from the category (to.e.vah), through its quality (bdelugma), to its embodiment (bdeluktos), to its consequences (exclusion at multiple levels).

**[CHAR-4]** E — The full arc (to.e.vah as abomination-verdict on idolatrous practice + shiq.quts as the detestable idol-object + bdelugma as the sacrilegious desolation-event) reveals a semantic range spanning: (1) the divine-verdict on idolatrous practices (to.e.vah — what the practices are before God); (2) the specific objects of misdirected devotion (shiq.quts — the idol-objects as detestable things); (3) the relational-covenantal betrayal dimension (to.e.vah in Deu 32:16 context — abominations provoking jealousy); (4) the eschatological-sacrilegious event (bdelugma — the abomination of desolation). The arc moves from the individual inner attachment (the heart going after shiq.quts objects) through communal practice and divine-verdict (to.e.vah) to cosmic-eschatological culmination (bdelugma tēs erēmōseōs). The vocabulary arc covers the full scope of the characteristic from inner devotion to eschatological judgment.

**[CHAR-5]** E — The full arc (a.ven spanning emptiness-iniquity-trouble + ro.a naming evil-quality-of-deeds + po.al a.ven naming the evildoer-person-type) reveals a semantic range covering: (1) the inner moral vacuity that generates harm (a.ven's root meaning of empty-yet-troubling); (2) the active cognitive-volitional scheming process (a.ven in VCG-02 — devising, plotting, conceiving); (3) the evildoer as a recognisable habitual-character class (po.al a.ven in VCG-03); (4) the accumulated inner condition (a.ven harboured — VCG-04); (5) the expressed quality of harmful deeds (ro.a — VCG-05); and (6) the trouble that lands on victims (a.ven in VCG-01). The vocabulary arc is remarkably comprehensive: from the root emptiness through the inner process to the character class to the accumulated condition to the expressed deeds to the victim's received trouble. The entire harm-cycle — from inner vacuity to social impact — is captured within the a.ven/ro.a vocabulary field.

**[CHAR-6]** E — The full arc (blasfēmeō as harm-speech + kakopoios as evil-doer person-type + atopos as legally irregular wrongdoing) reveals a semantic range covering: (1) the defiant cosmic-scale speech of the hardened will against God (blasfēmeō — VCG-01); (2) the social-communal defamation of God's name through moral failure and misrepresentation (blasfēmeō — VCG-02); (3) the hostile false accusation of the innocent as evildoers (kakopoios — VCG-03); (4) the formal legal charge of wrongdoing (atopos + kakopoios — VCG-03). The vocabulary arc covers the full range from cosmic-eschatological defiance of God (Rev 13:6; 16:9/11/21) through social community defamation (VCG-02) to intimate legal-charge false accusation (VCG-03). The characteristic operates across all scales of social reality — cosmic, communal, and judicial.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's full vocabulary arc — from ra.sha (wicked person-type) through to.e.vah/shiq.quts (abomination vocabulary) through a.ven (iniquity-scheming) to ponēros/kakia/adikia (constitutional evil nature) to blasfēmeō/kakopoios (evil expressed through speech) — reveals a comprehensive lexical map of inner evil across six dimensions: identity, abhorrence-verdict, active process, constitutional structure, and speech-expression. The arc moves from OT Hebrew (person-type and iniquity vocabulary) through the shared abomination vocabulary to NT Greek (constitutional evil and blasphemy vocabulary). The semantic range of the full cluster is thus: who the evil person is (Char 1), what God's verdict on their moral character is (Chars 3/4), what their inner faculties are generating (Char 5), what they are constituted as at the structural level (Char 2), and what their inner wickedness produces through speech (Char 6). The arc is complete — no dimension of inner evil's inner-being expression is unaddressed by the cluster's vocabulary.

**[CHAR-1]** E — The full vocabulary arc (H2930A verb → H2931 adjective → H5079 nid.dah → G0169 akathartos) reveals the characteristic as: (1) a dynamic event (verb — acquisition) and a static condition (adjective — state); (2) a paradigm-case bodily impurity (nid.dah — the menstrual/separation paradigm governing all bodily-discharge impurity); (3) a categorical conviction operative in conscience (akathartos in the NT categorical register). The arc reveals that the characteristic spans from the most granular bodily-mechanism level (specific discharge types, specific contact pathways) through the categorical-systemic level (the comprehensive clean/unclean taxonomy) to the conscience-formation level (the inner conviction that shapes the person's categorical perception of persons and things). The full semantic range is bodily → categorical → conscience.

**[CHAR-2]** E — The vocabulary arc (H2931 metaphorical-inner → G0167 akatharsia → G3435 molunō → G3436 molusmos → G3394 miasmos) reveals the characteristic's complete semantic range as: (1) constitutional human moral uncleanness before God (H2931 — inherited condition); (2) the habitual moral inner condition of impurity as a prior-master over the will (G0167 akatharsia); (3) the act of soiling or defiling the inner moral integrity (G3435 molunō); (4) the defilement as a penetrating condition of body and spirit (G3436 molusmos — 2Cor 7:1); (5) the defilement arising from passion-driven desire combined with contempt for authority (G3394 miasmos — 2Pe 2:10). The full arc: constitutional → habitual-dispositional → act-of-defiling → constitutional-penetration → passion-contempt complex. The range encompasses the characteristic from its deepest origin (constitutional inherited condition) to its most specific articulation (passion-driven defilement of the will).

**[CHAR-3]** E — The vocabulary arc (H2930A ta.me verb → H2931 ta.me adj → H5079 nid.dah) reveals the characteristic's complete semantic range as: (1) the act of defiling (ta.me verb — both self-defilement and external defilement of sacred spaces); (2) the resulting condition of being defiled (ta.me adj — persons, names, spaces declared unclean); (3) the quality of moral repugnance that the defilement-state generates in God's perception (nid.dah — the community's conduct as morally revolting as menstrual impurity). The full arc: act → condition → repugnance. The characteristic is thus not merely a legal category (defiled/not defiled) but a moral-relational reality that produces divine revulsion (Eze 36:17 nid.dah metaphor) and that requires divine action (Zec 13:1 — fountain of cleansing) for resolution.

**[CHAR-4]** E — The vocabulary arc is narrow and focused: G0169 akathartos as the character-descriptor of an external spiritual agent (pneuma akatharton), accompanied by healing vocabulary (iaomai — cured; therapeuō — healed) naming the structural opposite in its dynamic form. The full arc reveals: the characteristic is defined entirely by the agent who produces it rather than by the condition of the person who bears it. The healing vocabulary confirms the restoration as the telos. The arc is: unclean agent → condition produced in person (inferred from narrative) → healing restoration.

**[CLUSTER]** E — The cluster's full vocabulary arc — from the ta.me verb (H2930A — the act of defiling) through the ta.me adjective (H2931 — the condition of being unclean), nid.dah (H5079 — the paradigm-case physiological impurity/separation), akatharsia (G0167 — the habitual moral-inner impurity), molunō/molusmos (G3435/G3436 — the act and condition of soiling in body and spirit), miasmos (G3394 — the passion-driven defilement complex), and pneuma akatharton (G0169 compound — the external adversarial agent) — reveals the M10c domain's comprehensive semantic reach: act → condition → paradigm-case → habitual-state → soiling → passion-vehicle → constitutional-penetration → adversarial-agent-character. The arc begins at the most dynamic (acquiring defilement through act), passes through the most static (the condition as state), and ends at the most externally constituted (the agent's character as the defining vocabulary). The arc's breadth — from the most bodily and individual to the most spiritual and external — confirms the M10c cluster as a domain of remarkable range: one fundamental concept (incompatibility with holiness) operating across every dimension of creaturely existence.

questions.question_text: What is the function of the primary term within its primary verse -- (a) what role does it play in the sentence, and (b) what role does it play in the verse's own argument, if a connective/chain edge shows one?
questions.review_note: NOT fully Stage 1 — sentence-role half is Stage 1 (via verse_lexical/morph_code); argument/premise-conclusion half is a real, unowned gap (connective/chain notes give local edges only, nothing assembles them into an argument map). Wording already split in-place into (a)/(b) clauses (escalation #1444 v9, 2026-09-04), no new question_code.

findings.session_b_note:
The primary verse is identified as Luk 7:47 (Q043 answer) — the verse of highest inner-being density in the corpus:

"Therefore I tell you, her sins, which are many, are forgiven — for she loved much. But he who is forgiven little, loves little."

**Grammatical function:** The primary term (afiēmi) appears in the perfect passive: "are forgiven" (apeontai). The perfect tense signals: the act is complete and its effects are present. The passive voice signals: forgiveness has been received, not achieved. The verb functions as the **explanatory premise** of the clause — the woman's love (the observed fact) is explained by the forgiveness she has received (the interpretive reality). The term carries the entire causal weight of the sentence.

**Argumentative function:** The verse functions as a **causal argument**: observed behaviour (love) ← explained by invisible inner reality (forgiveness received). The argument moves from outer evidence to inner cause. The primary term is the pivot — it names the invisible inner event that makes the observable outer behaviour intelligible.

**Within the broader argument:** Luk 7:36-50 — the Pharisee host doubts Jesus's authority on the basis of the woman's moral history; Jesus's argument (the two-debtor parable, then the woman's actions, then the declaration) culminates in Luk 7:47 as the synthesis: the love visible in her actions is evidence of the forgiveness invisible to the Pharisee. The term "forgiven" is the argumentative climax.

findings.session_b_note:
For the primary programme anchor (2Cor 12:9, group 888-001): charis functions as the divine statement of sufficiency — the counter-assertion to Paul's request for relief. The term carries the weight of the entire argument: God's grace is the sufficient and complete response to weakness. In Eph 2:8 (888-001 second anchor): charis functions as the instrumental/causal basis of salvation — "by grace you have been saved" — the dative/instrumental of means, making grace grammatically the agent of the saving act.

*Consistent with prior analysis. Adds T7 framing.*

findings.session_b_note:
The primary active term is G4697 splanchnizō, and the primary anchor verse selected for this analysis is Matt 9:36: "When he saw the crowds, he had compassion for them (splanchnizō), because they were harassed and helpless, like sheep without a shepherd."

**Grammatical function:** Splanchnizō is the main verb of the clause — it is the central action of the sentence. Jesus saw (aorist participle — prior action); he was moved with compassion (aorist indicative — the main event); the following clause (Matt 9:37-38 — the harvest/prayer saying) and context (Matt 10:1 — the commissioning of the twelve) are the consequences. The compassion-verb is the structural hinge of the pericope: it is the inner event that explains and generates everything that follows.

**Argumentative function:** The verse functions as an explanation and motivation for both the harvest teaching (Matt 9:37-38) and the mission commissioning (Matt 10:1). The argument structure is: Jesus saw the condition of the crowds → was moved with compassion → declared the harvest great and the labourers few → commissioned the twelve. The compassion-event is the logical ground of the missional response. This makes splanchnizō not merely an emotional footnote but the theological engine of the entire pericope.

**The simile:** "like sheep without a shepherd" identifies the condition that triggered the compassion-movement: not primarily physical suffering but spiritual destitution — lostness, leaderlessness, vulnerability. This specifies which of the four semantic domains (T7.1 Prompt 3) is operative here: compassion toward spiritual destitution.

findings.session_b_note:
The primary anchor verse is Psa 51:17: "The sacrifices of God are a broken spirit; a broken and contrite heart, O God, you will not despise."

H1794 da.khah ("contrite") functions in this verse as a **qualifying predicate** — it modifies "heart" to specify the condition of the heart that God will not despise. The verse's logic is: the true sacrifice → is the broken spirit → specifically, the broken and contrite heart → which God will not despise. Da.khah ("contrite") is the precise characterisation of the heart's condition — the broken spirit is further specified as broken *and* contrite: crushed, ground down, not merely cracked or bent.

The term's function in the verse's logic is to name the quality of inner brokenness that constitutes genuine sacrifice — a qualitative descriptor that raises the stakes from general brokenness to specific contrite-crushing.

findings.session_b_note:
The registry carries two anchor verses for its largest group (873-001): Phili 3:10 and 1Jo 1:3. The anchor verse for the broadest definitional group is 1Jo 1:3 (as the verse most fully expressing the horizontal-vertical fellowship structure).

**1Jo 1:3:** *that which we have seen and heard we proclaim also to you, so that you too may have fellowship with us; and indeed our fellowship is with the Father and with his Son Jesus Christ.*

The term koinōnia (fellowship) functions *twice* in this verse: first as the telos of the proclamation (*so that you too may have fellowship with us*) and second as the constituting reality that grounds the proclamation (*our fellowship is with the Father and his Son*). The term functions as:
1. **The goal of the communicative act** (proclamation exists to create fellowship)
2. **The constituting ground of the capacity to extend it** (we can offer fellowship because ours is with God)

The verse's argument structure: *we have seen and heard → we proclaim → you may have fellowship with us → because our fellowship is with the Father and Son*. Fellowship is both the purpose of proclamation and the ground of its possibility.

findings.session_b_note: Mic 6:8 as primary definitional anchor: H2896A (tov — good) functions as the predicate of the divine definition: "He has told you, O man, what is good." findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-067-007: T7 as a whole reveals a characteristic whose evidential foundation is both exceptionally strong in some dimensions and genuinely constrained in others. Lexically: three OWNER terms across two language…
findings.finding_value: T7 as a whole reveals a characteristic whose evidential foundation is both exceptionally strong in some dimensions and genuinely constrained in others. Lexically: three OWNER terms across two languages with distinct semantic ranges, a full root-family analysis, a NT coinage (agathōsunē), and a comprehensive vocabulary arc from phenomenological breadth (H2896A) to virtuous precision (agathōsunē) to relational precision (chrēstotēs — Q&A-177). The lexical evidence is rich. Literary: the primary anchor (Mic 6:8) uniquely combines revelatory and covenantal-obligation frames with an internal tri-fold structure that no other verse replicates (Q&A-183); the anchor corpus spans prophetic, wisdom, psalmic, and epistolary forms across multiple contextual settings (Q&A-181). Human science: virtue ethics is the closest parallel framework, with the critical divergence at the source of goodness (divine gift vs natural achievement — Q&A-186). Constraints: NO_WORD_ANALYSIS flags on both Greek OWNER terms limit the LXX analysis (Q&A-175); LSJ data is absent. The evidential foundation is strong at the lexical-semantic and verse-literary levels; it is constrained at the LXX-continuity and human-science elaboration levels. This asymmetry is itself an analytic finding — it identifies where future investigation would most strengthen the registry's evidential base.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-022: T3's finding that goodness has an inherently perceptual character — it must be encountered and tasted, not merely inferred (Q&A-068) — is confirmed and grounded by T7's lexical and literary analysis. …
findings.finding_value: T3's finding that goodness has an inherently perceptual character — it must be encountered and tasted, not merely inferred (Q&A-068) — is confirmed and grounded by T7's lexical and literary analysis. The Psa 34:8 primary verse functions literarily as an invitation to perceptual encounter (Q&A-178) — "taste and see" is the literary form that corresponds to the T3 perceptual faculty engagement. The phenomenological root of H2896A (Q&A-168 — begins with concrete experience of what is agreeable and beneficial, rises to moral categories) explains why T3's perceptive faculty is so prominently engaged: the Hebrew root of goodness is itself experiential-perceptual before it is ethical-conceptual. T7's etymological grounding explains the T3 perceptual finding: the vocabulary encodes the experiential mode of knowing goodness that T3's faculty analysis confirms.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-067-025: T4 confirmed that the God-to-human direction of goodness is initiatory, generous, and sustaining (Q&A-101). T7 confirms that the primary literary form carrying divine goodness (prophetic covenantal ad…
findings.finding_value: T4 confirmed that the God-to-human direction of goodness is initiatory, generous, and sustaining (Q&A-101). T7 confirms that the primary literary form carrying divine goodness (prophetic covenantal address at Mic 6:8, doxological Psalm declarations, Pauline epistolary) all use forms that emphasise divine initiative and human receptivity. T7's literary analysis (Q&A-178-179) reveals that the literary forms carrying goodness are theologically intentional: the covenant lawsuit form (Mic 6:8) establishes divine initiative in defining the good; the invitation form ("taste and see" — Psa 34:8) establishes divine initiative in the encounter; the indicative-imperative structure of Col 3:12 (God has made you chosen → therefore put on kindness) establishes divine prior action before human response. T7's literary analysis confirms T4's relational architecture through the literary forms that carry them: the literature itself models the God-initiates-human-responds structure.

findings.session_b_note: Identifying 1Jo 4:8 ('God is love') as the primary theological claim and Joh 15:13 as the primary ethical-definitional verse: In 1Jo 4:8: the predicate nominative construction ('God is love') makes love not merely an attribute of God but an identification — love as God's being. The verb 'is' (estin) establishes identity, not activity. In Joh 15:13: 'greater love has no one than this: that someone lay down his life for his friends' — love is the subject of a comparative superlative; the function is to name the outer limit of love by identifying its maximum expression (soul-giving). The primary term in both cases functions as the frame of reference against which all other love-instances are measured: Joh 15:13 defines love's maximum; 1Jo 4:8 defines love's origin. Together they establish the top and bottom of love's definitional range: what love ultimately is (God's being) and what love ultimately does (gives itself to death for the beloved).

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-103-007: Love's evidential foundation is the most comprehensive in the programme. The primary terms (chesed, agapē/agapaō, racham/rachamim, ahavah, dod, phileō) cover the full constitutional range: willed-cove…
findings.finding_value: Love's evidential foundation is the most comprehensive in the programme. The primary terms (chesed, agapē/agapaō, racham/rachamim, ahavah, dod, phileō) cover the full constitutional range: willed-covenantal (chesed), Spirit-produced self-giving (agapē), somatic-compassionate (racham), intense-erotic (ahavah/dod), and naturally affective (phileō). The vocabulary structure itself distinguishes disposition/act/condition, received/given, and quality/person-type — making it architecturally precise. The semantic range of the primary terms spans from divine ontology (God is love) to moral inversion (love of darkness) — the widest semantic arc in the programme. The primary anchor is Lam 3:22 — love's most definitive affirmation precisely at the moment of maximum empirical falsification: a theological confession rather than an empirical observation. The LXX connection is partially evidenced (agapē as chesed-translated); full LXX analysis is limited by NO_WORD_ANALYSIS flags. The human science frameworks identified (attachment theory, virtue ethics) are named as Session D pointers but not elaborated — the instruction prohibits importing framework content not grounded in the data.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-103-018: The evidential foundation directly supports each of the three relational axes. GOD→HUMAN axis — most densely evidenced: Exo 34:6 (divine self-declaration of love as primary attribute), Jer 12:7 (belov…
findings.finding_value: The evidential foundation directly supports each of the three relational axes. GOD→HUMAN axis — most densely evidenced: Exo 34:6 (divine self-declaration of love as primary attribute), Jer 12:7 (beloved of God's soul), Mat 3:17 (beloved Son named), Joh 3:16 (God so loved the world), Rom 5:5 (love poured into hearts through Spirit). The lexical evidence for this axis runs from the OT's chesed-God group (169 active verses — largest single group in the registry, Q&A-038) through the NT's agapē-God group (35 relevant). HUMAN→GOD axis — Psa 63:3 (chesed above life), Mat 22:37 (total inner mobilisation), Joh 14:15 (love producing obedience); these are carried by the agapaō-love-of-God group (571-001) and the chesed-human group (536-002). HUMAN→HUMAN axis — Lev 19:18 (neighbour-love commandment), Mat 5:44 (enemy-love), Joh 13:34 (new commandment), Joh 13:35 (community identity); these span the rea-group (173 active), the agapaō-mutual group (571-004, 53 relevant), and the filadelfia group (558-001). The evidential foundation confirms that all three axes have strong lexical and verse-level grounding, with the GOD→HUMAN axis carrying the greatest evidential weight.

findings.finding_value: Reading T7 as a whole reveals the evidential foundation as both rich and gapped. The lexical foundation is comprehensive: mercy has terms for all grammatical roles (noun, verb, adjective, person-type), all operational aspects (disposition, act, seeking, structural opposite), and all major dimensions (compassion, covering, grace, propitiation, supplication). The vocabulary arc is itself a theological narrative (Q&A-180). The primary anchor verse is Psa 78:38 — the verse that most fully encodes the complete mercy-event structure (Q&A-185). The gaps are structural: LXX analysis and NT coinage data are unavailable (NO_WORD_ANALYSIS flag, 67 terms). Human science engagement identifies three relevant frameworks (moral psychology, attachment theory, shame theory) with the key divergence that the biblical model grounds mercy in prior reception rather than autonomous moral development (Q&A-189). The T7 synthesis: mercy's evidential base is wide and cross-genre (liturgical, prophetic, sapiential, narrative, epistolary) — this breadth confirms that mercy is not a sectional or contextual biblical theme but a structural reality appearing in every major literary context.

findings.finding_value: T7's vocabulary analysis shows supplication terms are a major category within R111 (H8467 techinah 24 active; H6279 atar 19 active; G2433 hilaskomai imperative in Luk 18:13). T4 shows the human-to-God direction is characterised by normative ongoing supplication (Q&A-107). Reading T4 and T7 together: the large volume of supplication vocabulary in T7's lexical analysis is the lexical quantification of T4's finding that mercy-seeking is the normative ongoing mode of the human-divine relationship. The vocabulary scale confirms the relational claim: if supplication were exceptional, there would be fewer terms; the 43 active supplication-vocabulary verses confirm ongoing, structured, habitual mercy-seeking. T7's grammatical range analysis (petition as the speech-mode of mercy, T1.4.3) maps to T4's human-to-God direction as the primary speech-mode context.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTRA-030-007: T7 as a whole reveals that the contrition vocabulary has a high degree of internal coherence and a sophisticated grammatical apparatus (distinguishing process, settled state, active/passive/volitional…
findings.finding_value: T7 as a whole reveals that the contrition vocabulary has a high degree of internal coherence and a sophisticated grammatical apparatus (distinguishing process, settled state, active/passive/volitional voice) that the English word "contrition" cannot render. The primary anchor verses (Isa 57:15, Psa 51:17) are architecturally complementary: Isa 57:15 provides the complete relational frame (divine character → divine dwelling → divine reviving); Psa 51:17 provides the inner-being substance (broken spirit, contrite heart as the acceptable sacrifice). The literary context (psalm and prophecy) requires reading the same characteristic in two modes: as human address to God (penitential psalm) and as divine address to the community (prophetic promise). The cross-testament gap (T7.1.8–9) is the methodological limitation — without LXX analysis the vocabulary arc from OT to NT cannot be closed from this registry's data. Human science frameworks confirm rather than challenge the biblical account, with the theocentric causality as the point of genuine divergence.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-018: The constitutional tier (T2) establishes spirit and heart as primary loci, bones as somatic expression; the evidential tier (T7) shows that these same loci are explicitly named in the primary anchor v…
findings.finding_value: The constitutional tier (T2) establishes spirit and heart as primary loci, bones as somatic expression; the evidential tier (T7) shows that these same loci are explicitly named in the primary anchor verses. The spirit/heart pairing in the verse evidence (Psa 34:18, Psa 51:17, Isa 57:15) and the bone imagery in Psa 51:8 are the exegetical ground for T2's constitutional account. T7 provides the textual evidence base from which T2 draws its constitutional conclusions. The two tiers are evidence-to-interpretation: T7 is the verse evidence; T2 is the constitutional interpretation of that evidence. Isa 57:15 as the primary anchor verse (T7) is also the verse that most completely names the constitutional event (T2): "contrite and lowly spirit... revive the spirit... revive the heart."

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-022: The faculty tier (T3) shows that contrition deepens conscience, moral evaluation, and cognition; the evidential tier (T7) identifies the primary literary form as penitential psalm and prophetic addres…
findings.finding_value: The faculty tier (T3) shows that contrition deepens conscience, moral evaluation, and cognition; the evidential tier (T7) identifies the primary literary form as penitential psalm and prophetic address — both forms that are constitutively about honest self-knowledge before God. The Psa 51 genre (penitential psalm — T7.2) is the literary vehicle for contrition in the conscience-and-cognition registers (T3.8, T3.9): the psalm form presupposes accurate self-assessment and directed it to God. The prophetic form (Isa 57:15, 66:2 — T7.2) is the vehicle for contrition in the volitional and relational registers (T3.6, T3.11). T7's literary analysis explains why T3 finds that different faculties are engaged in different evidential contexts.

findings.session_b_note: Cited as source by SYN-INTER-030-025: The relational tier (T4) shows the divine-to-human and human-to-God directions of contrition; the evidential tier (T7) identifies the primary literary contexts (penitential psalm = human-to-God; proph…
findings.finding_value: The relational tier (T4) shows the divine-to-human and human-to-God directions of contrition; the evidential tier (T7) identifies the primary literary contexts (penitential psalm = human-to-God; prophetic address = God-to-human). The literary forms in T7 directly correspond to the relational directions in T4: the psalm form is the human-to-God literary vehicle; the prophetic form is the God-to-human literary vehicle. The two primary anchor verses confirm this: Psa 51:17 (psalm — human addressing God in contrition) and Isa 57:15 (prophecy — God addressing the community with the promise of dwelling with the contrite). T7's literary analysis explains why T4 finds two distinct relational directions: they are embedded in two distinct literary genres.

The divine-to-human direction (T4.1) is primarily carried by the apostolic epistolary setting (2Pe 1:4, 2Cor 13:14, 1Jo 1:3). The human-to-God direction (T4.2) is primarily carried by wisdom poetry (Psa 119:63, Phili 3:10) and apostolic letter (Phili 3:10). The full vocabulary arc (from womb — most intimate — to almsgiving — most institutional) is unique in the programme: no other characteristic traverses this complete arc with equivalent lexical clarity. The CHASAD root includes shame as the negative semantic pole embedded within the compassion vocabulary itself — not an external antonym but an internal semantic component of the root family. The dual primary anchor finding (Hos 11:8 for divine compassion at constitutional depth; Luke 10:33 for human compassion as moral norm) establishes the two poles of the characteristic's evidential range. Three key argument structures: compassion-mission logic (Matt 9:36-10:1 — compassion as the theological engine of missional response), divine compassion-repentance ground (Joel 2:13 — divine character as the ground of human response-posture), Good Samaritan's moral logic (Luke 10:25-37 — compassion as the answer to "who is my neighbour?"). Three human science frameworks illuminate the vocabulary with genuine alignment (affective neuroscience, virtue ethics, attachment theory) and all three diverge from the biblical account at specific points (sovereignty vs automaticity; cross-boundary extension exceeding natural empathic scope; purposive suffering in Jas 5:11 requiring teleological frame). The LXX systematic analysis gap (NO_WORD_ANALYSIS flag on 98 terms) is the most significant methodological limitation — a new gap for the programme.

findings.finding_value: T3's perceptive-trigger and affect-mechanism findings are grounded in T7's primary anchor evidence. The Synoptic pattern of splanchnizō — always triggered by sight, always preceding action — is the textual ground for T3.1's finding (compassion is perceptively dependent) and T3.4's finding (affect is the mechanism of movement). T7's argument structure finding (Matt 9:36 — compassion as the theological engine of missional response) is the evangelist's literary expression of T3.10's analytical claim (compassion converts moral knowledge into motivated action).
